documents.title: Shared state-variable filter
documents.html:
NativeStateVariableFilter::new(sample_rate, Option<[f64;2]>) creates a CPU filter with fixed rate and two integrator states. state() supports exact continuation through another instance; sample_rate() reports the rate. process_sample(input,mode,cutoff,resonance) allocates nothing and commits state only when all computed states/outputs are finite. NativeSvfMode selects LowPass, HighPass, BandPass or Notch. Positive cutoff/sample-rate must be representable and at most 0.49, and resonance is 0..=1, with damping 2-1.9*resonance and Q=1/damping. These are the existing synth semantics.

process_into(input,output,mode,cutoff,resonance) accepts caller-owned equal-sized buffers and NativeFilterControl::Constant(value) or Samples(slice) controls. It allocates nothing, prevalidates complete input/control shapes and values, and caches coefficients for constant controls. Later arithmetic/cancellation errors may leave a committed output prefix and matching state; the remaining output suffix stays untouched. process(input,mode,cutoff,resonance) allocates its returned vector and stages the filter so failures leave the original state unchanged. BASIC SVFILTER uses that transactional variant. The block work cap is 32 units per sample within the existing 10-million-unit budget; the list cap is one million entries. Sample processing and block checkpoints observe native cancellation. These bounds do not establish a hard-real-time scheduling contract.

The native synth and this API call one shared recurrence. The synth retains its existing 20 Hz lower clamp and modulation controls; this numerical API accepts lower positive frequencies for scientific work and rejects out-of-domain input. It neither smooths abrupt parameter changes nor guarantees stability under every modulation sequence. Binary64 intermediate overflow is an error in the checked math API, even where a differently scaled computation could remain finite.

The recurrence follows the existing topology-preserving filter, with background in Cytomic's state-variable filter derivation. Independent fixed-parameter tests prewarp the analog cutoff before using SciPy's bilinear transform, which does not prewarp automatically. Modulated references solve the two nodal equations independently at each sample. See tools/check-svf.py and programs/science/modulated_filter.bas.

suffix stays untouched. `process(input,mode,cutoff,resonance)` allocates its
returned vector and stages the filter so failures leave the original state
unchanged. BASIC `SVFILTER` uses that transactional variant. The block work cap
is 32 units per sample within the existing 10-million-unit budget; the list cap
is one million entries. Sample processing and block checkpoints observe native
cancellation. These bounds do not establish a hard-real-time scheduling contract.

The native synth and this API call one shared recurrence. The synth retains its
existing 20 Hz lower clamp and modulation controls; this numerical API accepts
lower positive frequencies for scientific work and rejects out-of-domain input.
It neither smooths abrupt parameter changes nor guarantees stability under every
modulation sequence. Binary64 intermediate overflow is an error in the checked
math API, even where a differently scaled computation could remain finite.

The recurrence follows the existing topology-preserving filter, with background
in [Cytomic's state-variable filter derivation](https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/SvfLinearTrapOptimised2.pdf).
Independent fixed-parameter tests prewarp the analog cutoff before using
[SciPy's bilinear transform](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.signal.bilinear.html),
which does not prewarp automatically. Modulated references solve the two nodal
equations independently at each sample. See `tools/check-svf.py` and
`programs/science/modulated_filter.bas`.

documents.title: Flexible inverse actions for native linear operators
documents.html:
NativeLinearOperator::flexible_gmres(b,rtol,atol,max_iterations,initial,restart,&mut preconditioner) accepts the same borrowed FnMut(&[f64], &mut [f64]) -> Result<(), Error> output contract as gmres_with_preconditioner. The linear operator stays fixed. The inverse action may be nonlinear or change between invocations. Flexible right preconditioning retains each z=P(v), applies A(z), and reconstructs corrections from those retained z vectors. No interpreter Value allocation is required by the native API. The old fixed-left solver retains its existing behavior.

The shared Arnoldi/rotation implementation checks the original residual on every candidate. It admits at most two million combined V/Z elements and 100 million charged solver operations; operator and inverse callbacks share 10,000 calls. The right inverse is called once per attempted iteration and never for an already solved initial state or a zero-iteration request. Native callback work/side effects remain caller-owned; errors and cancellation propagate and input slices are not modified. Requested restart is 1–128, with the combined basis limit checked before allocation. BASIC exposes the same kernel as MFFGMRES with scoped DEF FN adapters.

documents.title: Robust geometry and reusable simple polygons
documents.html:
Crate-root NativeGeometry exposes orientation_2d(a,b,c), orientation_3d(a,b,c,d) and segment_relation_2d(a,b,c,d) on borrowed-by-value fixed arrays of finite coordinates. Orientation returns Result<i8,Error>; segment relation returns NativeSegmentRelation2::{Disjoint,Touch,Crossing,Overlap}. Predicates allocate no heap storage. Exact-input signs use the shared fixed-limb product accumulator; exact comparison-only paths cover axis-aligned 2D edges. The general 2D normal-range filter falls back near zero or outside its safe range. Triple-product signs evaluate the translated determinant through original-coordinate products, avoiding overflowing coordinate subtraction.

NativePolygon2::new(Vec<[f64;2]>) validates and owns a finite simple polygon with 3–4096 vertices, accepting an optional repeated closing point. Its immutable vertices() and orientation() accessors expose retained geometry. area(), signed_area(), perimeter() and locate([x,y]) reuse this validation; location is NativePointLocation2::{Outside,Inside,Boundary}. Queries allocate nothing and observe cancellation. Construction uses bounded quadratic edge-pair validation; measurement/location are linear in the vertex count. A failed query leaves the polygon available for reuse. The matching BASIC functions use exactly these kernels. See the language reference for shape, underflow/overflow and boundary contracts. No solid-mesh/CAD validity is implied by this polygon API.

documents.title: Polygon centroids and triangulation
documents.html:
NativePolygon2::centroid() -> Result<[f64;2],Error> returns the uniform-area centroid using exact accumulated moments/area and the shared symbolic/numerical ratio rounder. Work is linear; temporary big integers are bounded by the fixed binary64 accumulator widths and the 4096-vertex limit. Unlike area/perimeter/ location queries, centroid calculation allocates bounded temporary storage.

NativePolygon2::triangulate() -> Result<Vec<[usize;3]>,Error> returns n-2 nondegenerate faces referencing the retained zero-based vertices(). Winding and every original straight-edge vertex are preserved. It uses array-backed adjacency and blocking-vertex counts with a deterministic ear set, O(n) storage and fewer than 4*n*n point visits after validation. Boundary containment uses exact predicates, including points on prospective diagonals. Cancellation checks occur at outer updates and at most 256 point visits apart; no cross-platform wall-time guarantee is implied. All intermediate results are local, so failure leaves the immutable polygon reusable. BASIC uses the same methods and converts only the triangle indices to its usual one-based convention. Holes, quality meshing, solid validation and CAD interchange remain open.

documents.title: Indexed triangle surfaces and extrusion
documents.html:
NativeTriangleMesh3::new(Vec<[f64;3]>,Vec<[usize;3]>) owns a validated bounded triangle surface with zero-based Rust indices. vertices()/faces() borrow immutable slices, bounds() returns two coordinate triples, and topology() returns a copied NativeMeshTopology report. Its public fields are vertices, edges, faces, components, boundary_edges, nonmanifold_edges, winding_conflicts, nonmanifold_vertices and euler_characteristic. is_closed_oriented_manifold() checks indexed edge and vertex-link conditions. Open/non-manifold surfaces are admitted for diagnosis; invalid/degenerate inputs are rejected as described in the language reference. Coincident positions are not welded, and spatial self-intersection is not tested.

surface_area() -> Result<f64,Error> uses exact original-coordinate cross products with separate exponents, rounded scaled norms and exact accumulation. signed_volume() -> Result<f64,Error> checks closed oriented manifold topology, then rounds the exact determinant sum / 6 once. It is algebraic signed volume, not proof of an embedded physical solid. See the BASIC contract for units, rounding, overflow, topology limits, complexity and remaining solid-validity gates. Queries are cancellation-aware and leave the retained mesh reusable on failure.

NativePolygon2::extrude(height) -> Result<NativeTriangleMesh3,Error> creates a positive-height +Z extrusion using the same native polygon triangulation and mesh validation. Both polygon windings yield outward faces, with no new profile vertices; original straight-edge vertices are retained. This is reusable CPU backend construction, also exposed through BASIC POLYEXTRUDE3D.

documents.title: Exact triangle contacts and reusable mesh intersection index
documents.html:
NativeGeometry::triangles_intersect_3d([[f64;3];3],[[f64;3];3]) -> Result<bool,Error> classifies closed nondegenerate finite triangles, including boundary contacts, coplanarity and containment. Its scalar predicate path allocates no heap storage and constructs no rounded intersection coordinates. It reuses exact 2D/3D signs; coordinate-aligned 3D planes take an exact comparison/projection shortcut.

NativeMeshIntersectionIndex::new(&NativeTriangleMesh3) -> Result<Self,Error> borrows the immutable validated mesh and builds a balanced bounding-box hierarchy. The index retains face bounds/projection metadata and nodes, not copied geometry or interpreter values. Repeated queries reuse its O(F) storage. Lifetimes prevent mutation or dropping of the source mesh while it is borrowed.

intersections(NativeMeshIntersectionLimits { max_pairs, max_work }) returns NativeMeshIntersections { pairs: Vec<[usize;2]>, work, tested_pairs } only after complete enumeration. Each zero-based face pair is ascending and the list is lexicographically sorted. work counts node-pair plus leaf face-pair visits; tested_pairs counts face pairs with overlapping bounds that reach the exact predicate. Default limits are 10,000 pairs and 4,000,000 work, with admitted maxima 100,000/100,000,000. Zero limits are errors. Exhaustion discards partial output.

has_intersection(max_work) -> Result<bool,Error> stops at a proven first improper intersection. False requires completion. Both queries support cancellation and reuse after failure. Scanning uses a bounded-depth traversal stack and at most the admitted output budget; worst-case work remains quadratic despite spatial pruning. See BASIC contracts for shared indexed simplex semantics, cancellation/limits, spatial-versus-topological distinctions and remaining solid-domain requirements.

documents.title: Reusable closed solid domains
documents.html:
NativeSolidDomain3::new(&mesh, NativeSolidLimits) borrows an immutable NativeTriangleMesh3, validates closed consistently oriented manifold topology and exact nonintersection, then computes shell nesting and exact orientation. NativeSolidLimits has max_intersection_work and max_nesting_work, each default 4,000,000 and restricted to 1..=100000000; nesting work is shared by all shells. A single shell has depth zero without a containment scan. No geometry is welded, rounded, silently repaired or copied into interpreter values.

  • shells() borrows stable first-face-ordered NativeSolidShell records with zero-based first_face, faces, depth and exact orientation: i8 (-1/1). expected_orientation() alternates by depth; is_oriented() compares actual and expected orientation. The domain's is_oriented() checks every shell.
  • classify([x,y,z], max_work) returns `NativePointLocation3::{Outside,Inside, Boundary}`. The validated BVH and a fixed traversal stack make a single native query allocation-free. Exact predicates and symbolic projected tie-breaking cover boundary, shared-edge and vertex-ray cases without coordinate nudging.
  • classify_points(&points, max_work) allocates at most 100,000 classifications, reuses the same index and shares one work budget across the batch. It returns no partial result on error. Empty input is supported; each point must be finite.
  • volume() returns parity-filled material volume, with exact determinant accumulation/division and one binary64 rounding. It is independent of input whole-shell reversals; underflow may round to zero, final overflow errors.
  • oriented_faces() explicitly allocates corrected zero-based faces while preserving indices/order. Use the original vertices if constructing a new NativeTriangleMesh3. This only reverses entire validated shells.
  • nesting_work() reports the completed nesting phase's node/face visit count.

Index construction retains O(F) storage and O(F log F) balanced-tree work. Dense intersection/nesting/query cases still require explicit budgets. Admission, queries, volume and correction honor NativeCancellationToken; errors leave the borrowed mesh and completed domain reusable. BASIC MESHSHELLS3D, POINTINMESH3D, POINTSINMESH3D, MESHVOLUME3D and MESHORIENT3D use these same kernels and their one-based lists. Units, work-phase semantics, precision and manufacturing/model- format limits are specified in the language reference.

documents.title: Native STL geometry interchange
documents.html:
NativeStl::decode(&[u8], NativeStlFormat) -> Result<NativeStlDecoded,Error> performs bounded geometry parsing without filesystem access. Formats are Auto, Ascii and Binary; NativeStlFormat::parse accepts STL, STL-ASCII and STL-BINARY. The decoded structure owns mesh: NativeTriangleMesh3 and reports format, nonzero_attributes: usize and solid_blocks: usize. Mesh indices are zero-based. Exact coordinate welding preserves facet order/winding, normalizes signed zero, and performs no approximate repair. Supplied normals are advisory; nonzero binary attributes are counted without interpreting color conventions.

NativeStl::encode(&mesh, format, max_error) returns NativeStlEncoded { bytes: Vec<u8>, max_coordinate_error: f64 }. encode_with_limit(&mesh, format, max_error, max_bytes) additionally admits a smaller byte budget. NativeStl::MAX_BYTES is 64 MiB. Auto is invalid for export. ASCII round-trips binary64 coordinates. Binary conversion measures each exact absolute difference from the float32-rounded coordinate and refuses values above the explicit nonnegative finite allowance. Returned error is the largest actual coordinate difference. Overflow, collapsed faces and merging distinct indexed vertices are errors. ASCII also rejects distinct indices with equal coordinates.

NativeTriangleMesh3::face_normal(index) returns an approximate unit [f64;3] from shared exact cross-product components with exponent scaling. The index is zero-based; an invalid index errors. It handles finite extreme-coordinate faces without naive intermediate overflow or underflow. STL normal hints use the encoded geometry's winding, including after binary coordinate rounding.

Codec bounds are 100,000 facets, 200,000 unique vertices, 4,096 bytes per ASCII record and the byte cap. CPU work and storage grow with the bounded input; exact welding uses ordered maps. Cancellation errors discard incomplete results. No interpreter values, external providers or filesystem operations are required by these Rust APIs. BASIC MESH READ/WRITE applies the ordinary confined FileStore and transactional assignment/atomic replacement on top. Consult the language reference for grammar, metadata loss, units and solid-validation requirements. Revalidate binary-rounded geometry for spatial intersections; encoding does not promise preservation of every geometric separation or certify manufacturing.

documents.title: Shared color and alpha kernels
documents.html:
NativeColorMath accepts fixed binary64 arrays without interpreter values:

  • srgb_to_linear_channel(f64) and linear_to_srgb_channel(f64) implement the sign-reflected extended transfer; transform([f64;3], NativeColorTransform) converts triples. Enum variants are SrgbToLinear, LinearToSrgb, RgbToXyz and XyzToRgb. luminance([f64;3]) reads relative D65 Y from linear sRGB.
  • premultiply([f64;4]) and unpremultiply([f64;4]) convert alpha representation.
  • composite(source,destination,NativeColorComposite) and mix(first,second,t) consume and return straight linear RGBA. Alpha is coverage in [0,1]; RGB is finite, signed and unbounded by gamut. The twelve coverage enum variants and BASIC string spellings are listed in the language reference.
  • transform_batch(&[[f64;3]], transform) and composite_batch(&[[f64;4]], &[[f64;4]], operator) return owned typed vectors. MAX_COLORS=250000; composite lengths must match. Empty batches are valid. All public methods return Result<...,Error>, observe native cancellation and keep borrowed inputs unchanged. An error discards incomplete batch output.

Matrix arithmetic reuses exact pair-product accumulation. Weighted straight colors reuse the shared exact triple-to-pair ratio kernel, preserving HDR and subnormal-alpha contributions without intermediate overflow/underflow. Coverage factors are binary64 values, including rounded complements; returned alpha and color ratios round separately. An exact denominator of one takes a fixed-array triple-product route without heap allocation. Other ratios use bounded BigUint scratch; batches allocate output storage once, and do not construct interpreter values per pixel. Performance measurements apply to their recorded workloads.

There is no implicit byte quantization, gamut clipping, chromatic adaptation or renderer behavior change. Transfer powers are approximate; explicit premultiply can underflow and unpremultiply can overflow. See the BASIC contracts for exact zero-alpha semantics and precision/shape limits. The existing image/renderer adapters remain separate until their migration is qualified; these native APIs supply the common mathematical foundation for that work.

documents.title: Shared CPU image buffers and sampling
documents.html:
NativeRgbaImage owns row-major [f64;4] pixels in straight linear-light RGBA. Use checked new, filled, or from_rgba8(width,height,bytes,encoding); NativeImageEncoding::{Linear,Srgb} selects byte RGB transfer. RGB is finite signed/HDR; alpha is finite 0–1. pixels() borrows and into_pixels() consumes. NativeImageView::new(width,height,stride,pixels) validates active pixels and extent, ignoring padding; borrowed views carry no interpreter state. Width, height and stride are in pixels; pixel(x,y) checks integer indices.

A view supports:

  • sample(x,y,filter,border): pixel centers at x+.5,y+.5, with nearest or bilinear reconstruction and clamp/transparent borders; nonfinite coordinates are rejected, extreme finite coordinates are handled without integer overflow.
  • resize(width,height,filter,limits) and resize_rows(width,full_height,start,rows,filter,limits): nearest, linear, area-overlap or per-axis automatic filtering. Strips use the full output geometry and reproduce whole-image rows without materializing other strips.
  • mirrored(horizontal,vertical) and composite(destination,operator): immutable input, owned result, checked equal dimensions for compositing.
  • to_rgba8(encoding,clip): independent byte alpha and explicit out-of-gamut clipping or rejection. to_ppm(background,max_bytes) flattens in linear light, clips RGB, encodes sRGB, and returns bounded P6 bytes; no filesystem access.

Construction/full target geometry is capped at MAX_PIXELS=16_777_216. NativeImageLimits { max_samples } bounds planned source taps (default 100M, maximum 1B); it does not promise latency. Typed callers own aggregate memory admission. BASIC uses the existing shared asset budget, including old/new buffers during replacement. Native strip processing avoids a full output allocation; scratch does not retain a per-pixel sampling plan. Exact weighted sums/ratios may traverse the footprint repeatedly and use bounded integer scratch; checkpoints inside every traversal support NativeCancellationToken. No partially populated output escapes on failure/cancellation.

Weights/geometry are binary64. For each output, alpha is the exact weighted alpha sum divided by the exact weight sum, rounded to binary64; RGB is the exact weighted premultiplied numerator divided by exact weighted alpha. Rounded-zero alpha produces transparent black. Identical colors are preserved; same-size and nearest copies/mirroring preserve hidden RGB. This defines the arithmetic for computed weights, not exact rational source-cell geometry or ideal reconstruction. Area filtering reduces aliasing in shrinking images but is not a general frequency-optimal filter. The API adds no ICC, tone mapping, convolution, projective warp, tracing or inferred 3D reconstruction claim.

documents.title: Image-to-geometry bridge
documents.html:
NativeImageView::trace_regions(channel,threshold,limits) returns NativeImageContours; getters expose rings, selected_pixels, and boundary_edges. Each NativeImageContour provides vertices and signed_area. NativeImageChannel selects straight linear RGB, alpha or D65 luminance. NativeImageTraceLimits { max_edges } defaults to 100,000 and caps at 1,000,000. The walk constructs oriented selected-cell edges, removes shared interior edges, and turns right at diagonal contacts. A byte per image pixel holds membership and traversal state. It performs bounded linear scans/walks with checkpoints; collinear unit edges become corners. Signed integer cell-area sums are exact within the bounded dimensions. No partially traced result escapes.

Foreground has four-neighbor connectivity, background eight; boundaries are implicitly closed and can touch/revisit vertices. Area sign and ordering do not supply a parent-hole tree or guarantee simple polygons. No tolerance-based smoothing or inferred geometry is performed. trace_memory_bound(limits) is a conservative byte admission estimate including BASIC value conversion; typed callers may use it with their own aggregate memory budget.

height_mesh(channel,origin,spacing,height_scale) returns NativeImageSurface. mesh() borrows the shared NativeTriangleMesh3, uv() borrows matching normalized pixel-center UVs, and into_parts() transfers both. height_mesh_counts() preflights dimensions and the shared NativeTriangleMesh3::{MAX_VERTICES,MAX_FACES} caps. Full finite XY/Z coordinates use exact pair-product sums rounded once; positive XY spacing must survive rounding without collapse. Two triangles per cell share a consistent upper-left/lower-right diagonal and +Z orientation. Native mesh construction checks finite/nondegenerate geometry and indexed topology. The XY grid origin denotes the first input sample center; UVs instead normalize image-edge coordinates. The returned surface is open and retains no image borrow. These contracts support explicit height/depth fields and terrain/relief data; photo calibration/reconstruction, masking holes, adaptive tessellation, closed solids and renderer UV consumption remain distinct work.

documents.title: Linear circuit descriptors (2026-10-26)
documents.html:
NativeCircuit::new(nodes, Vec<NativeCircuitElement>) owns an immutable sparse linear model E*x' + G*x = B*u. Variants are Resistor {p,n,ohms}, Capacitor {p,n,farads}, Inductor {p,n,henries}, CurrentSource {p,n}, VoltageSource {p,n}, Vccs {p,n,cp,cn,siemens}, Vcvs {p,n,cp,cn,gain}, Cccs {p,n,control,gain} and Ccvs {p,n,control,ohms}. Native control is a zero-based element index. Nodes remain physical labels 0..N, with 0 ground.

matrices() borrows canonical native CSR G/E/B. node_count, unknown_count, elements, branch_indices (zero-based Option<usize>) and source_elements (zero-based) describe ordering without interpreter values. residual(x,dx,u) uses shared exact product sums across all three terms; jacobian(cj) returns G+cj*E. Its canonical pattern may change; fixed-pattern KLU consumers must account for that. Source amplitudes are external, and models can be borrowed by independent native consumers without retained mutable solver state.

dc(&[f64], NativeCircuitSolver) and ac(hz, &[BasicComplex], solver) return NativeCircuitSolution<T> {state,residual,backward_error,solver}. Solvers are Auto/Dense/Sparse; Dense uses the shared Rust real matrix kernel, AC an equivalent real block system, and Sparse the existing optional UMFPACK CPU provider. Physical residual and componentwise backward error are checked after row equilibration. This is numerical backward-error evidence, not a conditioning certificate.

memory_bound(nodes,elements) bounds model assembly/retention; solve_memory_bound(solver,ac) gives conservative working-set admission. Native callers enforce aggregate budgets; BASIC uses its shared asset reservations. Limits: 2,048 physical unknowns, 10,000 elements, 128 real dense equations (64 AC unknowns), sparse provider fill/work limits and scoped cancellation. Nonzero coefficient underflow/scaling loss, overflow, invalid topology or failed residual checks return errors. No regularizing ground conductance is silently added.

tests/circuit_tests.rs composes the assembled RC descriptor with NativeIda::integrate_with_jacobian, checking the exponential charging response and KCL. Static semiconductor and bounded index-one circuit transient APIs are described below; general higher-index reduction remains open. Conventions follow Qucs modified nodal analysis; implementation uses the project's existing sparse and exact-accumulation kernels.

Circuit solves may apply at most two iterative correction solves against exact physical-equation residuals, retaining only improvements. This controls loss of accuracy from row scaling in mixed-unit AC networks. A final componentwise backward error above 1E-10 still fails; the tolerance is never loosened.

documents.title: Static semiconductor kernels and nonlinear circuit operating points
documents.html:
NativeJunctionModel::new(Is, emission, kelvin) validates positive finite actual- temperature parameters. evaluate(volts) returns NativeJunctionSample {current, conductance}. voltage_scale() is n*k*T/q, using the SI Boltzmann/charge constants and shared exact product-ratio arithmetic. expm1 preserves small signals and logarithmic evaluation avoids overflowing exp(V/nVT) when the final current is representable. Unrepresentable current/conductance returns an error; very small reverse-bias conductance can round to zero. No limiter changes this device law.

NativeBipolarModel::new(transportIs,betaF,betaR,kelvin) implements reciprocal static Ebers–Moll with unity junction emission factor. evaluate([Vc,Vb,Ve],pnp) returns NativeBipolarSample {currents:[f64;3], jacobian:[[f64;3];3]}. Terminals are C/B/E; currents enter the device and Jacobian columns differentiate those voltages. In NPN polarity let F=Is*expm1((Vb-Ve)/VT), R=Is*expm1((Vb-Vc)/VT). Then Ic=F-(1+1/betaR)*R, Ib=F/betaF+R/betaR and Ie=R-(1+1/betaF)*F. PNP mirrors voltages and currents. Stable summation keeps reciprocal transport, base currents and analytic derivatives coherent without subtracting a rounded alpha from one. Is is supplied at the actual temperature; there is no hidden material/nominal-temperature law or semiconductor charge model.

NativeCircuitElement adds Diode {p,n,model}, Npn {c,b,e,model} and Pnp {c,b,e,model}. Bipolar terminals may coincide except all three at one node. is_nonlinear() distinguishes models requiring a bias. matrices() still borrows the linear G/E/B contribution; complete equations are E*x'+G*x+i_nonlinear(x)=B*u. residual includes devices and jacobian_at(state,coefficient) returns dF/dx+coefficient*E. Existing stateless dc, ac and jacobian reject nonlinear models. ac_at(hz,inputs,bias,solver) solves incremental phasors with the analytic Jacobian at the caller-supplied bias.

operating_point(inputs,initial:Option<&[f64]>,NativeCircuitDcOptions) returns NativeCircuitOperatingPoint: state/residual, scaled residual and step, Newton iteration/evaluation/source-step/backtracking counts, actual solver and accepted source fractions. Options/defaults and tolerance units match CIRCUIT OP in the language reference. Every success solves the unmodified full-amplitude circuit; failures return no partial operating point. Source stepping is bounded and explicit in the report. It is not a proof of existence, uniqueness or stability.

The same immutable model composes directly with NativeIda: use residual and jacobian_at callbacks with explicit variable IDs/consistent initial conditions. Tests compare diode-capacitor charging with a closed-form transformed exponential, static device currents/derivatives with 80-digit references and biased amplifier responses with independently differentiated models. Charge-aware semiconductor models and broader circuit transient workflows remain open.

Conventions/reference methods: Qucs nonlinear DC analysis and the ngspice diode equations. The implementation uses the existing Rust exact accumulators, canonical CSR, real linear solver, optional CPU UMFPACK and native IDA interfaces.

## Static semiconductor kernels and nonlinear circuit operating points

`NativeJunctionModel::new(Is, emission, kelvin)` validates positive finite actual-

and shared exact product-ratio arithmetic. `expm1` preserves small signals and
logarithmic evaluation avoids overflowing exp(V/nVT) when the final current is
representable. Unrepresentable current/conductance returns an error; very small
reverse-bias conductance can round to zero. No limiter changes this device law.

`NativeBipolarModel::new(transportIs,betaF,betaR,kelvin)` implements reciprocal
static Ebers–Moll with unity junction emission factor. `evaluate([Vc,Vb,Ve],pnp)`
returns `NativeBipolarSample {currents:[f64;3], jacobian:[[f64;3];3]}`. Terminals
are C/B/E; currents enter the device and Jacobian columns differentiate those
voltages. In NPN polarity let F=Is*expm1((Vb-Ve)/VT), R=Is*expm1((Vb-Vc)/VT).
Then Ic=F-(1+1/betaR)*R, Ib=F/betaF+R/betaR and Ie=R-(1+1/betaF)*F.
PNP mirrors voltages and currents. Stable summation keeps reciprocal transport,
base currents and analytic derivatives coherent without subtracting a rounded
alpha from one. Is is supplied at the actual temperature; there is no hidden
material/nominal-temperature law or semiconductor charge model.

`NativeCircuitElement` adds `Diode {p,n,model}`, `Npn {c,b,e,model}` and
`Pnp {c,b,e,model}`. Bipolar terminals may coincide except all three at one node.
`is_nonlinear()` distinguishes models requiring a bias. `matrices()` still borrows
the linear G/E/B contribution; complete equations are
`E*x'+G*x+i_nonlinear(x)=B*u`. `residual` includes devices and

`operating_point(inputs,initial:Option<&[f64]>,NativeCircuitDcOptions)` returns

documents.title: Circuit storage coordinates and bounded native transients
documents.html:
NativeCircuit::storage_layout() constructs NativeCircuitStorageLayout with parents(), differential(), mass_matrix(), from_physical(x) and to_physical(y). Ordinary index-one models retain the capacitor-only forest, algebraic common-mode roots and differential inductor currents. Reduced models use voltage-first forests and signed inductor cycle coordinates as described below. No floating rank threshold is used. Physical state is x=T*y; the mass matrix is E*T with prescribed derivative columns removed. Component stamps are transformed before exact accumulation so shared-diagonal rounding cannot invent a common-mode capacitance. Coordinate transformation admits at most 250000 stored path/CSR entries and 10000000 contribution operations per matrix transformation. Canonical zero entries are omitted. Layouts retain no mutable solver or BASIC objects.

NativeCircuitWaveform::{Constant,Sine,Table} and NativeCircuitKnot {time,left,right} make source discontinuities explicit. validate() checks domains/size; value(time,right) selects a knot's right or left limit. Between knots, interpolate from the previous right value to the next left value; outside hold endpoint values. Native construction permits validation at the API boundary, not unchecked indexing through the public value method.

NativeCircuit::transient(times,sources,Option<initialPhysical>,options) returns NativeCircuitTransientResult {trajectory,steps,residual_evaluations, jacobian_evaluations,error_test_failures,segments,algebraic_iterations,layout}. Its trajectory contains only requested times and physical state vectors. Options/defaults, units, source ordering, work/admission bounds, right-limit semantics and explicit solver/state limits match the BASIC reference. Automatic initial bias uses the existing OP solver; explicit physical initial values retain stored capacitor differences and inductor currents while analytic IDA initialization corrects algebraic guesses. Every source interval reinitializes the shared IDA backend, retaining stored state. Zero-storage models instead use bounded operating points at the requested times; algebraic_iterations reports their total Newton work, with zero IDA steps and Jacobian-callback count. Work/tolerance conventions match the BASIC reference. Callbacks use the selected interval's smooth source continuation for IDA internal steps; no unseen later jump contaminates the left interval's interpolation.

The shared NativeIda::consistent_initial_conditions_with_jacobian(t0,tDirection, yGuess,ypGuess,options,residual,jacobian) API supplies analytic dense consistent initialization without integrating a trajectory. It reuses the exact callback validation and solver path used by integrate_with_jacobian. Differential values are retained, algebraic values and differential derivatives are corrected. The contract follows SUNDIALS IDA initial-condition calculation. A nonsingular, admissible index-one problem is required; no arbitrary higher-index reduction or regularization is inferred from a small residual.

Qualification: physical-coordinate matrix exponentials, independent orthogonal floating-capacitor reduction, damped RLC state space/energy, nonlinear Radau diode references, exact ramp/jump convolution, native/BASIC failure recovery and exported consumer parity. Evidence: output/circuit-transients-2026-10-26/validation.json once accepted. Matrix-free/Krylov circuit transients, higher-index reduction, state-triggered switching/recovery and charge-aware semiconductor models remain open, as do installed-OS/provider and physical-device acceptance.

storage_memory_bound() covers coordinate/CSR assembly and export without a solver. transient_memory_bound(samples) additionally admits the conservative AUTO OP working set as well as the selected dense or capped sparse IDA/output buffers. This covers optional initial bias and zero-storage sweeps before native providers are entered; BASIC target/model state and budget charges survive admission failure unchanged.

Structural sparse IDA and circuit transients

NativeIdaSparseJacobian::new(dimension,rowPointers,columnIndices,values) owns a square zero-based CSR pattern with finite values that may be exactly zero. Dimensions are 1–1024 and at most 250000 slots are admitted. Row pointers must span the slots, columns must be sorted and unique within each row, and values must be finite. Read-only accessors expose dimension, slot count, pointers, columns and values. This type is separate from NativeCsrMatrix, which retains its canonical nonzero-only contract.

NativeIda::integrate_with_structural_jacobian(times,y,yp,options,residual,jacobian) and consistent_initial_conditions_with_structural_jacobian(t0,direction,y,yp, options,residual,jacobian) accept callbacks returning this structural matrix. NativeIdaLinearSolver::Klu { nonzeros } specifies the slot count, including zeros. The matrix represents dF/dy + cj*dF/dyprime. Every callback must keep its shape, slot count and pattern; a changed pattern fails before provider matrix storage is replaced. Both methods correct algebraic values and differential derivatives while retaining differential values. Direction time must differ from initial time; initialization alone does not integrate beyond it. Existing integrate_with_sparse_jacobian keeps its canonical-CSR/preconsistent-input contract. Provider allocation caps, cancellation, callback error propagation and work limits apply to both paths.

Circuit TRANSIENT selects dense IDA through 256 physical unknowns and structural KLU for 257–1024 unknowns. Topology-derived slots include every possible static junction contribution and transformed mass entry; zeros/cancellations do not change the pattern or perturb the physical equations. Coordinate multiplication accumulates only touched columns, without a dense temporary matrix. All source intervals and final-time jumps use analytic sparse consistent initialization. The conservative admission bound includes the 64 MiB KLU factor cap, structural buffers, output cells and possible AUTO operating-point work. Actual memory is measured separately. The KLU-enabled provider must be present; no large dense fallback is attempted.

Qualification: output/sparse-circuit-transients-2026-10-26/validation.json, with independent heterogeneous sparse RC exponentials, floating-capacitor orthogonal reductions, nonlinear Radau references, RLC state-space references, a 1024-state native workload, source jumps, zero coefficients, cancellation/recovery and interpreter/export parity. Higher-index reduction, matrix-free preconditioning, state switching, restart, charge-aware devices and OS/hardware gates remain open.

Independent-source circuit constraint reduction

NativeCircuitStorageLayout additionally exposes coordinate_matrix() (T), inverse_coordinate_matrix(), source_coordinate_matrix() (S), source_derivative_matrix() (D), stored_source_matrix() (H) and prescribed(). The shared reduced residual is F(T*y,0,u)+mass*yprime+D*uprime=0; marked coordinates satisfy y(k)=(S*u)(k). Matrix row/column identities and BASIC CONSTRAINTS serialization are defined in the language reference. Layouts retain only immutable sparse data, supporting direct native reuse.

Voltage-first incidence trees handle independent-voltage capacitor loops. Spanning trees of inductors between conductive components isolate prescribed current sums while retaining independent circulating currents. These operations use signed unit coefficients and exact accumulation. Raw capacitor stamps are transformed before rounding; the original capacitance/common-mode safeguards remain. Physical trajectories keep node/branch order, and explicit initial stored state is checked against source constraints before solver entry.

NativeCircuitWaveform::derivative(time,right) returns the analytic derivative of the chosen one-sided smooth piece. For a table value jump it does not include a distributional impulse. Table slopes divide exact differences, avoiding intermediate overflow/underflow. Only source derivatives actually used by D are evaluated by the transient engine. Smooth-piece continuation remains isolated across knots, and final-time slope corners receive right-hand initialization.

For zero free-state problems the existing physical Newton/continuation engine accepts D*uprime as an additional residual load. The public static operating-point API supplies zero load and keeps its existing behavior. Value and derivative loads are scaled together during continuation. H checks every relevant source jump, even between requested samples; nonzero stored-state jumps fail explicitly. Simultaneous common-mode jumps with unchanged stored state are allowed.

The topological distinction between CV loops and LI cutsets, and the need for additional controlled-source conditions, is discussed in Cortes Garcia et al., topological MNA decoupling. The incidence path reduces independent-source constraints. The controlled-source extension below also uses exact linear algebra; it is not an implementation or claim of the paper's full controlled-source theorem. Pure independent source loops and floating/current-only components remain explicit errors. All admitted controlled/nonlinear systems still require nonsingular numerical initialization. General nonlinear/higher-index reductions, impulse redistribution and full production/OS/hardware qualification remain open. Switching and restart have separate qualified contracts described below.

Evidence: output/circuit-constraints-2026-10-26/validation.json, including independent physical laws, constrained RLC matrix exponentials, diode loads, cycle-current preservation, source corners, explicit rejection/recovery, 1023-variable sparse resources and BASIC/export parity.

Physical circuit checkpoint/restart

NativeCircuit::transient_with_checkpoint(times,sources,initial,options) returns (NativeCircuitTransientResult, NativeCircuitCheckpoint). The checkpoint is immutable and created only after a successful full trajectory. time(), state(), sources() and options() expose its saved right-hand physical state and inputs. to_bytes()/to_text() preserve all binary64 bits in the versioned bounded MBCIRCP1/MBCIR1 format. Model identity stores the complete canonical ordered component description, including all semiconductor and controlled-source parameters; no identity hash collision can silently accept another model.

model.restore_transient_checkpoint_bytes(bytes) and model.restore_transient_checkpoint(text) validate the entire record and exact model identity before returning a checkpoint. Length/count limits are checked before variable-size allocations, numerical/source/options invariants are checked, and native cancellation is polled during serialization and parsing. The FNV-1a corruption checksum provides no authentication; callers must apply their ordinary file provenance policy. Records contain data only. Binary size is capped at 1 MiB, aggregate table knots at 10000, individual tables at 1024 and transients at 1024 physical unknowns. The current format is explicit about right-hand source semantics.

model.resume_transient(times,&checkpoint) returns a new result/checkpoint pair. The first time must equal the saved absolute time; all source schedules and options are retained. It invokes the same constraint-aware, analytic dense/KLU integration and initialization path. There is no fresh DC equilibrium substitution for saved capacitor voltages or circulating inductor currents. Algebraic state is corrected consistently, as in ordinary explicit-initial transients. Solver-private adaptive history is reconstructed, so reference accuracy rather than identical internal steps is the qualification criterion. Limits apply per call; provider availability and numerical convergence are still required at resume.

checkpoint_text_size(sources) reports exact text length before solver entry; checkpoint_memory_bound(sources) adds conservative model/source, decode and export storage to the existing transient admission. BASIC ADVANCE/RESUME return the result and text together, preserve targets on failure and retain TRANSIENT compatibility. ## Circuit storage coordinates and bounded native transients

`NativeCircuit::storage_layout()` constructs `NativeCircuitStorageLayout` with
`parents()`, `differential()`, `mass_matrix()`, `from_physical(x)` and
`to_physical(y)`. Ordinary index-one models retain the capacitor-only forest,
algebraic common-mode roots and differential inductor currents. Reduced models
use voltage-first forests and signed inductor cycle coordinates as described
below. No floating rank threshold is used. Physical state is `x=T*y`; the mass
matrix is `E*T` with prescribed derivative columns removed. Component stamps are transformed before exact
accumulation so shared-diagonal rounding cannot invent a common-mode capacitance.
Coordinate transformation admits at most 250000 stored path/CSR entries and
10000000 contribution operations per matrix transformation. Canonical zero entries
are omitted. Layouts retain no mutable solver or BASIC objects.

`NativeCircuitWaveform::{Constant,Sine,Table}` and `NativeCircuitKnot {time,left,right}`
make source discontinuities explicit. `validate()` checks domains/size;
`value(time,right)` selects a knot's right or left limit. Between knots, interpolate
from the previous right value to the next left value; outside hold endpoint values.
Native construction permits validation at the API boundary, not unchecked indexing
through the public value method.

`NativeCircuit::transient(times,sources,Option<initialPhysical>,options)` returns
`NativeCircuitTransientResult {trajectory,steps,residual_evaluations,
jacobian_evaluations,error_test_failures,segments,algebraic_iterations,layout}`. Its trajectory contains
only requested times and physical state vectors. Options/defaults, units, source
ordering, work/admission bounds, right-limit semantics and explicit solver/state
limits match the BASIC reference. Automatic initial bias uses the existing OP
solver; explicit physical initial values retain stored capacitor differences and
inductor currents while analytic IDA initialization corrects algebraic guesses.
Every source interval reinitializes the shared IDA backend, retaining stored state.
Zero-storage models instead use bounded operating points at the requested times;
`algebraic_iterations` reports their total Newton work, with zero IDA steps and
Jacobian-callback count. Work/tolerance conventions match the BASIC reference.
Callbacks use the selected interval's smooth source continuation for IDA internal
steps; no unseen later jump contaminates the left interval's interpolation.

The shared `NativeIda::consistent_initial_conditions_with_jacobian(t0,tDirection,
yGuess,ypGuess,options,residual,jacobian)` API supplies analytic dense consistent
initialization without integrating a trajectory. It reuses the exact callback
validation and solver path used by `integrate_with_jacobian`. Differential values
are retained, algebraic values and differential derivatives are corrected. The
contract follows [SUNDIALS IDA initial-condition calculation](https://sundials.readthedocs.io/en/v6.6.0/ida/Usage/index.html).
A nonsingular, admissible index-one problem is required; no arbitrary higher-index
reduction or regularization is inferred from a small residual.

Qualification: physical-coordinate matrix exponentials, independent orthogonal
floating-capacitor reduction, damped RLC state space/energy, nonlinear Radau diode
references, exact ramp/jump convolution, native/BASIC failure recovery and exported
consumer parity. Evidence: `output/circuit-transients-2026-10-26/validation.json`
once accepted. Matrix-free/Krylov circuit transients, higher-index reduction,
state-triggered switching/recovery and charge-aware semiconductor models remain
open, as do installed-OS/provider and physical-device acceptance.

`storage_memory_bound()` covers coordinate/CSR assembly and export without a solver.
`transient_memory_bound(samples)` additionally admits the conservative AUTO OP
working set as well as the selected dense or capped sparse IDA/output buffers. This covers optional initial bias
and zero-storage sweeps before native providers are entered; BASIC target/model
state and budget charges survive admission failure unchanged.


### Structural sparse IDA and circuit transients

`NativeIdaSparseJacobian::new(dimension,rowPointers,columnIndices,values)` owns a
square zero-based CSR **pattern** with finite values that may be exactly zero.
Dimensions are 1–1024 and at most 250000 slots are admitted. Row pointers must
span the slots, columns must be sorted and unique within each row, and values
must be finite. Read-only accessors expose dimension, slot count, pointers,
columns and values. This type is separate from `NativeCsrMatrix`, which retains
its canonical nonzero-only contract.

`NativeIda::integrate_with_structural_jacobian(times,y,yp,options,residual,jacobian)`
and `consistent_initial_conditions_with_structural_jacobian(t0,direction,y,yp,
options,residual,jacobian)` accept callbacks returning this structural matrix.
`NativeIdaLinearSolver::Klu { nonzeros }` specifies the **slot count**, including
zeros. The matrix represents `dF/dy + cj*dF/dyprime`. Every callback must keep
its shape, slot count and pattern; a changed pattern fails before provider matrix
storage is replaced. Both methods correct algebraic values and differential
derivatives while retaining differential values. Direction time must differ
from initial time; initialization alone does not integrate beyond it. Existing
`integrate_with_sparse_jacobian` keeps its canonical-CSR/preconsistent-input
contract. Provider allocation caps, cancellation, callback error propagation
and work limits apply to both paths.

Circuit TRANSIENT selects dense IDA through 256 physical unknowns and structural
KLU for 257–1024 unknowns. Topology-derived slots include every possible static
junction contribution and transformed mass entry; zeros/cancellations do not
change the pattern or perturb the physical equations. Coordinate multiplication
accumulates only touched columns, without a dense temporary matrix. All source
intervals and final-time jumps use analytic sparse consistent initialization.
The conservative admission bound includes the 64 MiB KLU factor cap, structural
buffers, output cells and possible AUTO operating-point work. Actual memory
is measured separately. The KLU-enabled provider must be present; no large dense
fallback is attempted.

Qualification: `output/sparse-circuit-transients-2026-10-26/validation.json`, with
independent heterogeneous sparse RC exponentials, floating-capacitor orthogonal
reductions, nonlinear Radau references, RLC state-space references, a 1024-state
native workload, source jumps, zero coefficients, cancellation/recovery and
interpreter/export parity. Higher-index reduction, matrix-free preconditioning,
state switching, restart, charge-aware devices and OS/hardware gates remain open.


### Independent-source circuit constraint reduction

`NativeCircuitStorageLayout` additionally exposes `coordinate_matrix()` (T),
`inverse_coordinate_matrix()`, `source_coordinate_matrix()` (S),
`source_derivative_matrix()` (D), `stored_source_matrix()` (H) and `prescribed()`.
The shared reduced residual is `F(T*y,0,u)+mass*yprime+D*uprime=0`; marked
coordinates satisfy `y(k)=(S*u)(k)`. Matrix row/column identities and BASIC
CONSTRAINTS serialization are defined in the language reference. Layouts retain
only immutable sparse data, supporting direct native reuse.

Voltage-first incidence trees handle independent-voltage capacitor loops.
Spanning trees of inductors between conductive components isolate prescribed
current sums while retaining independent circulating currents. These operations
use signed unit coefficients and exact accumulation. Raw capacitor stamps are
transformed before rounding; the original capacitance/common-mode safeguards
remain. Physical trajectories keep node/branch order, and explicit initial stored
state is checked against source constraints before solver entry.

`NativeCircuitWaveform::derivative(time,right)` returns the analytic derivative
of the chosen one-sided smooth piece. For a table value jump it does not include
a distributional impulse. Table slopes divide exact differences, avoiding
intermediate overflow/underflow. Only source derivatives actually used by D are
evaluated by the transient engine. Smooth-piece continuation remains isolated
across knots, and final-time slope corners receive right-hand initialization.

For zero free-state problems the existing physical Newton/continuation engine
accepts D*uprime as an additional residual load. The public static operating-point
API supplies zero load and keeps its existing behavior. Value and derivative
loads are scaled together during continuation. H checks every relevant source
jump, even between requested samples; nonzero stored-state jumps fail explicitly.
Simultaneous common-mode jumps with unchanged stored state are allowed.

The topological distinction between CV loops and LI cutsets, and the need for
additional controlled-source conditions, is discussed in
[Cortes Garcia et al., topological MNA decoupling](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.20475v1).
The incidence path reduces independent-source constraints. The controlled-source
extension below also uses exact linear algebra; it is not an implementation or
claim of the paper's full controlled-source theorem. Pure independent source
loops and floating/current-only components remain explicit errors. All admitted
controlled/nonlinear systems still require nonsingular numerical initialization.
General nonlinear/higher-index reductions, impulse redistribution and full
production/OS/hardware qualification remain open. Switching and restart have
separate qualified contracts described below.

Evidence: `output/circuit-constraints-2026-10-26/validation.json`, including
independent physical laws, constrained RLC matrix exponentials, diode loads,
cycle-current preservation, source corners, explicit rejection/recovery,
1023-variable sparse resources and BASIC/export parity.


### Physical circuit checkpoint/restart

`NativeCircuit::transient_with_checkpoint(times,sources,initial,options)` returns
`(NativeCircuitTransientResult, NativeCircuitCheckpoint)`. The checkpoint is
immutable and created only after a successful full trajectory. `time()`, `state()`,
`sources()` and `options()` expose its saved right-hand physical state and inputs.
`to_bytes()`/`to_text()` preserve all binary64 bits in the versioned bounded
MBCIRCP1/MBCIR1 format. Model identity stores the complete canonical ordered
component description, including all semiconductor and controlled-source parameters;
no identity hash collision can silently accept another model.

`model.restore_transient_checkpoint_bytes(bytes)` and
`model.restore_transient_checkpoint(text)` validate the entire record and exact
model identity before returning a checkpoint. Length/count limits are checked
before variable-size allocations, numerical/source/options invariants are checked,
and native cancellation is polled during serialization and parsing. The FNV-1a
corruption checksum provides no authentication; callers must apply their ordinary
file provenance policy. Records contain data only. Binary size is capped at 1 MiB,
aggregate table knots at 10000, individual tables at 1024 and transients at 1024
physical unknowns. The current format is explicit about right-hand source semantics.

`model.resume_transient(times,&checkpoint)` returns a new result/checkpoint pair.
The first time must equal the saved absolute time; all source schedules and options
are retained. It invokes the same constraint-aware, analytic dense/KLU integration
and initialization path. There is no fresh DC equilibrium substitution for saved
capacitor voltages or circulating inductor currents. Algebraic state is corrected
consistently, as in ordinary explicit-initial transients. Solver-private adaptive
history is reconstructed, so reference accuracy rather than identical internal
steps is the qualification criterion. Limits apply per call; provider availability
and numerical convergence are still required at resume.

`checkpoint_text_size(sources)` reports exact text length before solver entry;
`checkpoint_memory_bound(sources)` adds conservative model/source, decode and export
storage to the existing transient admission. BASIC ADVANCE/RESUME return the result
and text together, preserve targets on failure and retain TRANSIENT compatibility.
Qualification: `output/circuit-restart-2026-10-26/validation.json`, with native dense/
sparse/constrained models, malformed-frame/cancellation/admission tests, fresh-process

controlled-source reductions and production/OS/hardware gates remain open.

from those voltages would lose charge. Native `storage_coordinates()` exposes the

documents.html:
NativeSurfaceMath::perspective_weights([f64;3],[f64;3]) and interpolate<const N:usize>(barycentric,clip_w,[[f64;N];3]) return checked perspective weights/attributes. N is 1–16; barycentrics are finite nonnegative with positive total and clip W is finite positive. Exact four-product numerator and three-product denominator sums avoid forming reciprocals or rounded weights; each attribute is rounded once from the ratio of the supplied binary64 inputs. lambert(normal,light,ambient) safely normalizes finite nonzero directions and returns artist-controlled ambient-plus-positive-cosine gain. It is not a physical BRDF. shade(albedo,texel,gain) accepts finite straight linear HDR RGBA, alpha 0–1 and finite nonnegative gain; exact RGB triple products avoid intermediate range loss. Nonfinite final results fail. These calls observe native cancellation.

NativeTriangleMesh3::normal_of_triangle([[f64;3];3]) shares the checked exact-coordinate normal used by face_normal. It rejects nonfinite/collinear vertices and avoids overflowing coordinate differences or underflowing crosses. NativeImageView::sample_uv(u,v,filter,border) adds normalized image-edge UVs, top-left origin and downward V. Pixel centers are ((x+.5)/w,(y+.5)/h). NEAREST/LINEAR and CLAMP/TRANSPARENT are supported; nonfinite UVs fail.

The actual CPU mesh renderer uses these kernels for OBJECT IMAGE bindings. A bound immutable image and its asset reservation share ownership; replacing or releasing a named image cannot invalidate or stop accounting for its texture. This is an opt-in linear rendering path; existing byte texture behavior remains. Evidence: output/surface-math-2026-10-26/validation.json. The corner-normal API below extends this bridge with smooth shading. Remaining limits include alpha cutouts, existing raster edge/depth precision, no blended transparency, antialiasing or physical light transport.

## Shared surface interpolation and material math

`NativeSurfaceMath::perspective_weights([f64;3],[f64;3])` and

range loss. Nonfinite final results fail. These calls observe native cancellation.

documents.title: Corner normals and smooth surface transforms
documents.html:
NativeTriangleMesh3::corner_normals(crease_radians) returns Vec<[[f64;3];3]>, indexed by face then corner. Crease is finite 0–pi; zero returns flat normals. Otherwise consistently wound two-face indexed edges join corner fans when their rounded normal angle is at most the crease. Components are local-edge connected fans, not global angular clusters. Boundary, nonmanifold and conflicting-winding edges remain hard; duplicate positions and vertex-only contacts are not welded. Exact sums of oriented coordinate crosses provide area weighting before a scaled norm. Undefined zero fan sums fail. This is not angle weighting or geometry subdivision. Native cancellation and existing mesh bounds apply; storage is linear in faces plus an edge sort.

NativeSurfaceMath::oriented_normal(normal,linear_matrix) returns the normalized cofactor map using exact scaled triple-product sums. It preserves indexed winding through reflections and accepts rank-two transforms only when the particular mapped normal stays nonzero. This differs in sign from unsigned inverse-transpose normal conventions under reflection. Nonfinite/zero inputs or zero mapped results fail. MESHCORNERNORMALS3D and NORMALTRANSFORM3D expose these kernels to BASIC.

OBJECT NORMALS consumes generated or authored corner normals in the actual CPU renderer, including clipping, perspective-correct normal interpolation, linear material/texture shading and atomic failure. Per-face normals add 72 bytes within the 100,000-face scene cap. Evidence: output/smooth-surface-2026-10-26/validation.json. Flat rendering remains available; antialiasing, blended coverage, subdivision, shadows and physical light transport remain separate work.

NativeTrigonometry::sin_cos_phase(time, frequency, phaseRadians) returns [sin(2*PI*time*frequency+phaseRadians), cos(...)] for finite inputs. It reduces the exact 106-bit dyadic product to a quadrant and residual using fixed-size integer arithmetic, without a potentially overflowing floating product or heap allocation for reduction. Signed time/frequency are accepted. Radian offsets use libm sin_cos on the original offset, then checked product accumulation for composition. Exact zero-offset quarter-cycle axes, nearby residuals and representable subnormal sines are retained. This is a binary64 kernel, not a correct-rounding or relative-error certificate for arbitrary phase cancellation. NativeCircuitWaveform::Sine value/derivative paths reuse it; genuine amplitude or derivative overflow remains an error. The source-only host qualification is recorded in output/phase-waveforms-2026-10-26/validation.json.

Crate-root NativeTrigonometry provides checked sin_cos_pi, sin_pi, cos_pi, tan_pi, sinc_pi, sin_cos_degrees, sin_degrees, cos_degrees, tan_degrees, sech, csch, angle_between3([f64;3],[f64;3]) and signed_angle2([f64;2],[f64;2]). Pairs are [sine,cosine]; vector outputs are radians. BASIC calls and both sinc resamplers share the same kernels. Exact axis reduction, hyperbolic subnormal tails and scaled exact-product vector angles are specified in Trigonometry. Existing BasicReal and BasicComplex expose radian elementary functions and principal complex branches. Scalar phase work does not allocate; exact vector accumulators use bounded storage.

Real ACOSH and native NativeTrigonometry::acosh use a cancellation-free log1p expression near one, shared with BasicReal::acosh. This preserves accuracy for inputs immediately above the real domain endpoint.

Real ATANH, BasicReal::atanh and NativeTrigonometry::atanh share an odd- symmetric log1p path, preserving tiny inputs and accuracy near both +/-1 boundaries. Inputs on or beyond those real boundaries remain errors.

documents.title: Shared global quadrature
documents.html:
Crate-root NativeQuadrature::integrate(callback,lower,upper,options,breakpoints) accepts FnMut(f64)->Result<f64,Error>, NativeQuadratureOptions and a borrowed finite breakpoint slice. NativeQuadratureReport exposes value, estimated_absolute_error, evaluations, intervals and typed NativeQuadratureStatus; as_str() matches BASIC QUADINT statuses. FNINT reuses the same kernel with its legacy scalar/error contract. See the language manual for exact defaults, limits, statuses and domain limitations.

A worst-error heap drives refinement. Existing exact accumulators retain global value/error/floor updates without rescanning or losing cancellation. Quadrature weights, callback values and bounds use exact triple products before rounding. Allocation is bounded by the validated panel cap (40 bytes per heap element, up to 65536 reserved elements) plus up to 4097 bounds and fixed panel scratch. Each initial panel costs 15 callback evaluations; each completed bisection adds 30 and one retained panel. Cancellation checkpoints surround each callback and refinement. Arbitrary native callbacks are not preemptible and their side effects are not transactional. Scalar integrands must remain deterministic during a call.

These are heuristic error estimates for finite binary64 real arguments, without infinite bounds, principal values, extrapolation or certified enclosures. A non-converged report is diagnostic data, not an accepted answer; callback/domain failures return Err. Original interval endpoints are not sampled. An initial interval without 15 distinct interior nodes is rejected before callbacks.

documents.title: Shared scalar differentiation
documents.html:
Crate-root NativeDifferentiation::differentiate(callback,point,options) accepts FnMut(f64)->Result<f64,Error> and NativeDerivativeOptions. NativeDerivativeDirection is Central, Forward or Backward. NativeDerivativeReport exposes value, estimated_absolute_error, step, evaluations, iterations and typed NativeDerivativeStatus with as_str() matching BASIC. DERIVATIVE and automatic NDERIV consume this same implementation. NativeDifferentiation::central_difference(callback,point,step) preserves the fixed two-sample contract used by explicitly stepped NDERIV, without an error estimate. See the language manual for all defaults, limits and failure behavior.

The adaptive path uses bounded four-neighbor and center stencils, normalized actual sample coordinates, degree-four interpolation and exact weighted callback differences through the existing product-ratio accumulator. A fixed 256-radius history bounds revisits. Integer arithmetic in the exact ratio helper has fixed input sizes; no storage grows with callback count. Checkpoints surround every callback and trial. At most 4097 callback attempts and 256 trials are admitted. Native callback internals cannot be preempted; callbacks must be deterministic and own their side effects. Recoverable off-center domain failures may be retried, so an error is not a promise that the callback ran only once.

Error estimates combine successive estimates, bilateral consistency for central sampling and a conservative floating sample-roundoff model. They are not proof bounds and cannot establish differentiability or identify every aliased/noisy function. Higher-order, vector/Jacobian and certified symbolic work are separate.

documents.title: Shared bounded scalar searches
documents.html:
Crate-root NativeScalarSearch::root(callback,lower,upper,options) returns NativeRootReport with point, value (the sampled residual), lower/upper bounds, lower_value/upper_value, evaluations, iterations and NativeScalarSearchStatus. NativeScalarSearch::extremum(callback,lower,upper,options,kind) accepts NativeScalarExtremum::Minimum or Maximum and returns NativeExtremumReport with point, value, lower/upper bounds, evaluations, iterations and status. Both take FnMut(f64)->Result<f64,Error> and NativeScalarSearchOptions; their BASIC consumers are ROOTFIND/MINFIND/MAXFIND and the legacy scalar wrappers. See the language manual for exact defaults, limits and report contracts.

Root secants use exact triple/pair ratios; bisection ensures interval contraction without discarding a sign bracket. Extrema use exact parabolic coordinate ratios with golden fallback, reusing three objective samples and recalculating the current coordinate interpolation to avoid accumulated golden-grid drift. Interval-width acceptance uses exact product signs. Fixed-size scalar state and bounded exact-ratio arithmetic do not grow with iteration count. Checkpoints surround callbacks and each iteration; arbitrary callback internals and side effects remain the caller's responsibility.

Continuity and strict unimodality are assumptions, not properties inferred from finite samples. Evaluated zero, interval acceptance, grid exhaustion, objective resolution and detected sample-shape contradictions are separate statuses. Floating callback noise can still mislead every finite-sampling method. These APIs do not complete general nonlinear solving or global optimization.

Hysteretic circuit switching

NativeCircuit::switched_transient(times,sources,switches,initial,options) uses NativeCircuitSwitch (zero-based resistor index, voltage-control nodes, low/high thresholds, finite positive on/off resistances and initial boolean mode) and NativeCircuitSwitchOptions { transient, maximum_events }. It returns NativeCircuitSwitchedResult { transient, events, final_modes, event_evaluations, final_coordinates }. Event switch indices are zero-based in Rust and one-based in BASIC. Each event retains physical before/after states and its new mode. The immutable caller model is unchanged and errors return no partial trajectory.

The same capacitor/inductor coordinate map is retained in every mode. Analytic Jacobian consistency solves hold differential storage coordinates fixed, then resolve algebraic state/derivatives and any zero-time threshold cascade in caller order. Scheduled source corners partition smooth intervals. Purely algebraic circuits add an internal differential clock, removed from public outputs. A fixed structural pattern includes resistor slots that cancel to zero in one mode. NativeIda::integrate_hybrid_with_structural_jacobian exposes that zero-slot hybrid KLU path to other Rust consumers too; its initial state and derivatives must already be consistent. Existing canonical-CSR APIs retain their contract.

Nested native KLU projections share the outer allocation cap and provider; they cannot obtain another allowance. Depth is limited to 16. A nested request for a smaller limit is rejected because it cannot retroactively bound outer live allocations. Guards normalize against their active threshold, preventing a remote inactive threshold from collapsing a nonzero guard. Aggregate work and retained-state admission remain bounded by the circuit API.

This checkpoint covers finite resistive switching and supported index-one circuits. Exact event isolation, arbitrary ideal topology changes, impulses, installed provider/hardware acceptance remain open. Current evidence: output/circuit-switching-2026-10-26/validation.json.

Portable switched circuit continuation

NativeCircuit::switched_transient_with_checkpoint(times,sources,switches,initial,options) returns (NativeCircuitSwitchedResult, NativeCircuitSwitchedCheckpoint). resume_switched_transient(times,&saved) returns the same pair. Its first time must equal the saved absolute time. Recreate the exact ordered base circuit to resume in another process; switch resistance overrides do not modify that model.

The immutable checkpoint exposes time(), state(), storage_coordinates(), sources(), switches(), modes() and copied options(). Original switch configuration includes original initial modes, while modes() reports the current settled modes. Both are preserved across repeated saves. Physical and reduced coordinates are retained together to preserve stored charge/current hidden by floating-point rounding at large common modes. The internal clock of a purely algebraic circuit is reconstructed and never serialized.

Use to_bytes()/restore_switched_checkpoint_bytes(bytes) for MBCSWCP1 binary, or to_text()/restore_switched_checkpoint(text) for uppercase-hex MBCSW1 text. The outer record carries a bounded ordinary state codec, original switch specs, current modes and event budget, with separate version/checksum validation. Ordinary MBCIR1 records remain unchanged and cannot be used as switched records. switched_checkpoint_text_size(sources,switches) preflights exact output length; switched_checkpoint_memory_bound supplements the integration memory allowance. Both native and BASIC paths enforce the 1 MiB binary cap, bounded fields, finite parameters, exact model identity and physical/reduced/prescribed-state consistency. A checksum is corruption detection, not authentication.

Resume rebuilds IDA history and consistency with saved modes/reduced state; results are numerical continuations, not bit-identical solver histories. Step, event and work budgets restart for each call. Topology/device support and event resolution limits remain those of switched_transient. BASIC SWITCHADVANCE and SWITCHRESUME consume these same native methods. Qualification evidence: output/switched-circuit-restart-2026-10-26/validation.json.

Switch control voltages and restored-mode validation use one exact accumulation of both coordinate rows before rounding. This retains small stored control differences under large common-mode voltages and prevents false transitions caused by subtracting separately rounded node readings.

documents.title: Dynamic junction charge and circuit mass
documents.html:
NativeDynamicJunctionModel::new(junction,C0,Vj,M,Fc,TT) composes an existing NativeJunctionModel with depletion and diffusion charge. evaluate(volts) returns NativeDynamicJunctionSample { current, conductance, charge, capacitance, capacitance_slope }. The immutable original inputs are available through junction() and charge_parameters(). Parameter ranges, units, source model references and physical limitations are specified in the language manual's DQ section. The kernel handles the M=1 limit, small normalized voltages, scaled products and the capacitance-tangent join; no finite differencing is used.

NativeCircuitElement::ChargeDiode { p,n,model } contributes the static current plus C(v)*vprime to KCL. mass_matrix_at(state) returns the complete dF/dxprime. jacobian_at_rate(state,derivative,coefficient) returns dF/dx + coefficient*dF/dxprime, including C'(v)*vprime. Existing jacobian_at(state,coefficient) specifies a zero derivative. ac_at uses state-dependent capacitance; matrices() remains the constant linear G/E/B subset. A bias must come from an independently established operating point.

Retained-coordinate integration evaluates junction voltage differences before rounding individual physical nodes. This applies to static junction conduction as well as nonlinear storage. A differential coordinate preserves charge because supported capacitance is strictly positive. Source-prescribed coordinates use explicit waveform derivatives; pure algebraic sweeps include those displacement currents, and final source corners are reprojected. Structural KLU patterns include all junction slots independently of current numeric values. Dense/sparse Newton callbacks receive actual derivatives and one-sided source pieces. Existing bounded work, cancellation and memory policies apply; no BASIC callback evaluates a device equation.

Storage-layout mass and D maps describe only constant linear elements. Nonlinear mass/state-slope contributions are assembled in the solver; layout differential and prescribed-storage maps include charge diodes. Voltage jumps across a prescribed DQ imply an unsupported impulse. Hysteretic resistance changes preserve voltage/charge. Ordinary and switched portable records include exact DQ model parameters and retain the existing binary/text versions for compatible models. Native solver history is still rebuilt on resume.

BASIC exposes DQ rows, DEVICE sampling, derivative-aware JACOBIAN and bias-aware LINEARIZE using these same native methods. Current qualification evidence: output/circuit-charge-2026-10-26/validation.json. MOS and advanced bipolar devices, other semiconductor effects, general index reduction, ideal-switch impulses and broader engineering/OS/hardware gates remain open.

documents.title: Quasistatic bipolar charge
documents.html:
NativeDynamicBipolarModel::new(conduction,be,bc) accepts a NativeBipolarModel and two [C0,Vj,M,Fc,TT] arrays. conduction() and charge_parameters() retain those exact inputs. A zero C0/TT pair disables one branch; other parameters are still validated. evaluate([Vc,Vb,Ve],pnp) returns NativeDynamicBipolarSample { currents, jacobian, charges, capacitance, charge_hessian }, with collector/base/emitter axes. The last three fields are Q (C), dQ/dV (F) and d2Q/dV2 (F/V). Static conduction remains reciprocal Ebers–Moll. Diffusion uses transport current, and PNP mirrors the voltage and charge signs. No native solver state or BASIC value is retained by a model.

NativeCircuitElement::ChargeNpn {c,b,e,model} and ChargePnp participate in the same shared circuit analysis and checkpoint APIs. Their active BE/BC branches contribute separate stored-voltage edges. Tied terminals and disabled branches add no storage edge; exact common-mode differences survive retained coordinates. The shared mass, full-rate Jacobian, source forcing and structural sparse paths iterate both branches. Storage-export admission includes both rows in the prescribed-storage map. Model tags 14/15 serialize all 14 parameters; existing ordinary/switched record versions are unchanged.

BASIC NPNQ/PNPQ rows and DEVICE inspection expose the native model. Full units, parameter ranges, tensor axes and physical omissions are documented in the language reference. Independent laws, coupled AC, charge-balance trajectories, source corners, sparse/fresh-process persistence and native/export workloads are qualified in output/bipolar-charge-2026-10-26/validation.json. MOS models, base-width/high-injection effects, non-quasistatic transport, general index reduction and production/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.

Native constant-slope MOS charge sheet

NativeChargeSheetMosModel::new(threshold,beta,slope,kelvin,oxide_capacitance,body) validates the long-channel model above the shared native circuit engine. body is a NativeDynamicJunctionModel at exactly the same actual temperature, with positive zero-bias capacitance. parameters() returns the five core parameters; body_junction() returns the exact bulk model. evaluate([Vd,Vg,Vs,Vb],pmos) returns NativeMosSample { currents, jacobian, charges, capacitance, charge_hessian }, with four signed terminal axes and analytic derivatives. NativeCircuitElement::Nmos/Pmos { d,g,s,b,model } supplies direct Rust reuse; BASIC NMOSQ/PMOSQ and DEVICE expose the same implementation.

The full law, units, charge-reference threshold and limitations are specified in the language reference's Long-channel MOS terminal charge section. Implicit endpoint charge avoids exponential overflow in strong inversion; exact scaled ratios avoid intermediate slope/temperature overflow, with unrepresentable normalization derivatives rejected. A differential charge solve resolves small drain bias. Second derivatives produce the full rate-dependent transient Jacobian. Terminal derivatives obey current/charge conservation and reference-voltage invariance; the charge matrix is generally nonreciprocal. Bulk junctions use the existing bounded depletion/diffusion law.

Four-terminal structural stamps enter shared dense/KLU patterns, storage maps, source-rate loads, source-corner projection, switching and continuation. Storage coordinates retain differences relative to source before evaluation; this avoids reconstructing tiny gate/drain biases from rounded common-mode voltages. New model identity tags 16/17 store all twelve parameters and four nodes in ordinary/switched records. Earlier tags and record versions remain valid. No provider, GPU dependency or separate runtime engine is introduced.

Qualification includes independent 90-digit Lambert-W/charge-integral derivative references, CMOS inverter DC/AC/Radau charge balance, sparse and fresh-process continuation, cancellation, finite-input overflow errors and standalone parity. Evidence: output/mos-charge-2026-10-26/validation.json. Process fitting, advanced short-channel/body models, noise/thermal/NQS, general index reduction and physical hardware acceptance remain open.

Mathematical background: EPFL EKV model equations and terminal charge integrals. The implemented constant-slope approximation and its limits are specified above.

The CPU IDA bridge uses a Newton convergence coefficient of 0.03 for ordinary integration, keeping the supplied relative/absolute integration tolerances and algebraic error control intact. This addresses step stagnation observed in a strict-tolerance CMOS restart with a correct reduced residual/Jacobian. The variational-sensitivity API retains its explicit coefficient setting. Circuit and general IDA dense/sparse/event/initialization references are checked together; this solver setting is not an added physical effect in the MOS model. See SUNDIALS nonlinear convergence control.
