documents.title: Rational Bezier curves and conics
documents.html:
RBEZIER(coordinates,weights[,mode]) creates an editable {"RBEZIER1",coordinates,weights,mode} packet. The shared Rust type is NativeRationalBezier<2> or NativeRationalBezier<3>, with two to four controls (degree one through three). Modes are case-insensitive:

  • "WEIGHTED" (default): coordinates are Euclidean control points. The numerator controls are the exact products of those coordinates and their weights. Native construction is NativeRationalBezier::new(points,weights).
  • "HOMOGENEOUS": coordinates already are numerator controls; they are not multiplied by weights. A nonzero numerator with zero weight represents a control direction at infinity. Native construction is NativeRationalBezier::from_homogeneous(numerators,weights).

All coordinate/weight inputs must be finite, with one weight per control and at least one nonzero weight. Zero and negative weights are supported. These two representations are intentionally distinct: a zero weight removes a weighted Euclidean control's contribution, while a homogeneous zero-weight numerator can contribute a direction at infinity.

BASIC operationShared native operationResult
RBEZIERPOINT(curve,t)point(t)Two-/three-component point
RBEZIERDERIV(curve,t[,order])derivative(t,order)Original-parameter derivative; default order 1, supported 0–3
RBEZIERBATCH(curve,parameters[,order])evaluate_many(parameters,order)Input-order rows; default order 0
RBEZIERSAMPLE(curve,segments)sample_uniform(segments)segments+1 point rows with uniform parameter spacing
RBEZIERSPLIT(curve,t)split(t)Two child curves with parameters mapping to [0,t] and [t,1]

Native getters are coordinates(), weights(), is_homogeneous() and degree(). Parameters must be finite and inside [0,1]. There is no implicit extrapolation. Derivatives of a rational curve need not vanish above its numerator degree. The common curve fraction core evaluates the represented numerator and denominator exactly, forms quotient derivatives, and rounds only the returned components. This avoids premature weight-product overflow and rounded cancellation. Weighted endpoint points retain the original coordinates verbatim when their denominator is nonzero.

The exact represented denominator must be nonzero at every queried parameter. A zero denominator is an error, even for a removable 0/0; no epsilon cutoff or automatic limiting value is substituted. Signed weights can create poles and unbounded portions. Successful point or batch queries do not certify that the whole interval is pole-free. Uniform sampling is neither arc-length spacing nor a geometric error bound, and joining samples across an unqueried pole is unsafe. Positive weights provide the usual control-hull property in weighted mode.

Subdivision evaluates the homogeneous de Casteljau controls in exact arithmetic. Each returned weight and coordinate is rounded once. A child uses weighted coordinates where finite dehomogenization is possible, otherwise homogeneous coordinates retain its infinite controls. Splitting returns an error if a nonzero weight rounds to zero, all child weights vanish, or the chosen output representation cannot be finite. No common rescaling rescue is attempted. Subsequent queries use the rounded child data; repeated splitting can accumulate error and perturb denominator roots. Child derivatives use their new local parameters, so compare them with the parent's derivatives multiplied by the appropriate parameter-scale power.

Batches accept at most 65,536 parameters. Uniform sampling accepts 1–65,536 segments. The shared 65,536-bit reduced numerator/denominator bound limits exact arithmetic; intermediate temporaries can be larger. Traversals check cancellation, and batch/subdivision errors return no partial result. Final unrepresentable components raise RealOverflow. Editable BASIC packets require no registration or backend version changes.

For example, RBEZIER({{1,0},{0,1},{-1,0}},{1,0,1},"HOMOGENEOUS") represents the upper half of a unit circle without irrational input weights. The programs/science/rational_conic.bas consumer scales this construction into a 3D CAD ellipse and checks its tangents and subdivision. Definitions follow the Michigan Tech rational curve notes and the homogeneous circular-arc construction. No external implementation or new dependency is incorporated.

Qualification: exact Bernstein-polynomial and independent symbolic derivative references, conic identities, subdivision data, native/BASIC/export parity and resource/cancellation checks in output/rational-bezier-2026-10-26/validation.json when accepted. NURBS/rational surfaces, composite/arc-length workflows and broader CAD, math/application/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.

Exact rational-curve interval checks

RBEZIERDOMAIN(curve[,from,to[,maxRefinements]]) calls the shared Rust NativeRationalBezier::domain(from,to,NativeRationalDomainOptions). The default closed interval is [0,1]; explicit bounds must be finite, ordered and inside that interval. Subdivision budget defaults to 256 and accepts 0–4096. Zero requests exact counts with any unresolved intervals retained. BASIC applies its usual integer conversion to the budget (for example, 1.5 becomes 2); the native Rust option is an integer.

The result is freely readable BASIC data:

{"RDOMAIN1",{from,to},status$,refinements,counts,{intervals...}}
counts = {distinct,denominatorMultiplicity,removable,poles,poleMultiplicity}
interval = {lower,upper,"EXACT"|"OPEN",counts}

All counts refer to exact polynomials formed from the represented input coordinates and weights, including unrounded weighted products. distinct counts denominator zeros; denominatorMultiplicity includes repetition. A common polynomial GCD across every numerator and the denominator identifies cancellations. removable counts zeros fully removed by cancellation; poles counts the remaining distinct poles; poleMultiplicity sums their orders after cancellation (the largest remaining order across coordinates). A partially cancelled root remains a pole. Raw 0/0 is still undefined for point/derivative queries, so only zero denominator roots establishes a usable whole interval.

EXACT is a singleton exactly representable root. OPEN means roots lie strictly between the bounds; roots at either bound are reported separately. Reports cover the whole requested closed interval without duplicate endpoint counts. The status is:

  • REGULAR: no denominator zeros in the entire closed interval.
  • ISOLATED: every root is an exact singleton or is alone between adjacent binary64 bounds. These are enclosures, not rounded root estimates.
  • RESOLUTION_LIMIT: distinct roots share an adjacent-binary64 gap; exact counts and multiplicities are retained without claiming separate locations.
  • REFINEMENT_LIMIT: the budget ended with at least one wider interval. Counts remain exact; some other intervals may also contain unresolved clusters.

Root counting reuses the algebra engine's exact Sturm kernel with one-sided endpoint signs; multiplicities use repeated polynomial GCDs. The algebra certificate checker retains independent multiplication-identity verification. Curve coefficients retain the 65,536-bit reduced fraction bound; symbolic coefficients retain their existing 4,096-bit and charged-work policies. Domain checks additionally cap polynomial work at 2,000,000 charged steps. Cancellation or arithmetic/work exhaustion raises an error with no partial report. Binary64 bit-range subdivision bounds refinement even near subnormal parameters.

REGULAR certifies denominator absence only: it does not certify finite rounded coordinates, safe derivative magnitudes, geometric accuracy, or regular nonzero tangents. Edited or rounded subdivided curves must be checked again. NURBS, surfaces and composite arc-length workflows remain open.

programs/science/rational_domain.bas demonstrates a pole missed by uniform sampling and a checked conic. Qualification uses independent exact SymPy polynomials, GCDs and interval counts (SymPy polynomial reference), native/BASIC/export parity and resource/recovery checks. Evidence: output/rational-domain-2026-10-27/validation.json when accepted.

Adaptive rational-curve polylines

RBEZIERADAPT(curve,tolerance[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]]) calls NativeRationalBezier::sample(NativeCurveSamplingOptions) and returns:

{parameters,points,{maximumDeviation},status$}

The default limits are 4096 segments and depth 40. Rational sampling accepts 1–65,536 segments and depth 1–1074; the existing polynomial sampler retains its own depth limit of 52. BASIC uses its usual integer conversion for the limits. Tolerance must be positive and finite. Parameters cover [0,1] in increasing order, with one more point than segments. Each point is the same correctly rounded original-curve query returned by RBEZIERPOINT.

The finite deviation bounds the Euclidean distance from every exact curve point in each parameter interval to its corresponding rounded output segment. It is a geometric, one-sided bound. It does not bound same-parameter linear interpolation, tangent error, arc-length spacing, or the reverse distance from the segment to the curve. Nonlinear rational parameterizations of straight segments may therefore have a zero geometric bound.

The Rust implementation first performs an exact whole-interval denominator check. Any denominator zero, including removable 0/0 and endpoint zeros, raises an error before a polyline is returned. It then computes exact homogeneous Bernstein controls restricted from the original curve to each candidate interval. These are scratch values, not rounded child packets. If their nonzero weights have one sign, the curve is a convex combination of their dehomogenized controls. A zero weight with all-zero numerators contributes nothing; a zero weight with a nonzero numerator has no finite hull bound yet.

For each finite exact control, Rust projects onto the actual rounded output segment and computes an exact L1 residual. The largest residual conservatively bounds Euclidean distance over the whole convex hull, including endpoint rounding. The reported value rounds upward once. This also handles coincident endpoints and collinear backtracking without mistaking an infinite line for a finite segment. Mixed-sign controls or directions at infinity trigger refinement until a finite bound is established or a limit is reached. The nonnegative-weight convex-hull property supplies the geometric basis; common negative weight scales are equivalent.

CONVERGED means every segment's bound is at most the requested tolerance. SEGMENT_LIMIT and RESOLUTION_LIMIT retain a complete ordered polyline; the latter covers the requested depth or an unavailable distinct binary64 midpoint. Inspect the status before treating the tolerance as achieved. {maximumDeviation} is empty if no finite bound was established, including unresolved control weights or bound overflow. Limits return an estimate to inspect, not permission to claim accuracy.

The heap stores finite panel metadata and points, not a growing tree of exact controls. At most 2*maxSegments-1 panels are evaluated; exact scratch arithmetic retains the shared 65,536-bit reduced fraction limit. Cancellation is checked during refinement and homogeneous restriction. Arithmetic/work failure or an unrepresentable sampled coordinate raises an error with no partial result. A finite geometric certificate does not promise finite derivatives or regular tangents. Subnormal geometry and bounds may hit the final point-rounding floor.

Qualification includes independent exact change-of-variable Bernstein certificates, dense exact point-to-segment comparisons, compressed-parameter curves, homogeneous underflow, native resources/cancellation and interpreted/ exported BASIC parity. Consumer: programs/science/adaptive_conic.bas. Evidence: output/rational-sampling-2026-10-27/validation.json when accepted. NURBS/surfaces, composite continuity and arc-length parameterization, and broader application/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.

Certified rational-curve length

RBEZIERLENGTH(curve[,absTol[,relTol[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]]]]) calls NativeRationalBezier<N>::length(NativeCurveLengthOptions) for the complete 2D/3D linear, quadratic or cubic curve on [0,1]. It returns:

{value,{absoluteError},lowerBound,{upperBound},segments,status$}

Native fields have the corresponding snake_case names in NativeCurveLengthReport. Optional numbers are empty lists/None when no finite upper certificate has been established; then value=lowerBound and there is no accuracy claim. NativeCurveLengthStatus is CONVERGED, SEGMENT_LIMIT or RESOLUTION_LIMIT. Both bounds cover the whole path, including repeated traversal, even on a limit. The estimate is the rounded midpoint of a finite enclosure; absoluteError bounds its distance to either end. Only CONVERGED meets absoluteError <= max(absTol,relTol*abs(value)), compared without floating overflow/underflow.

Defaults are absolute and relative tolerances 1e-6, 4096 segments and depth

  1. Tolerances must be finite/nonnegative with at least one positive;

segments are 1..65536 and depth is 1..1074. BASIC integer options use the language's usual integer conversion. A supplied absolute tolerance alone leaves the default relative tolerance enabled; pass zero explicitly to disable it. Depth exhaustion or no interior binary64 midpoint reports RESOLUTION_LIMIT. Limits do not report success or silently omit intervals.

The engine first rejects every exact raw denominator zero on [0,1], including removable and endpoint zeros. Each panel restricts the original exact homogeneous data, with the same bounded Rust arithmetic used by sampling. For a finite same-sign control polygon, endpoint distance is a lower bound and control-polygon length is an upper bound. Mixed signs or a nonzero direction at infinity require refinement before providing that upper bound. Zero homogeneous controls contribute nothing.

Why the upper bound is valid: for normalized positive rational Bernstein weights lambda_i, put S_k=sum(i>k,lambda_i). Then S'_k=sum(j<=k<i,(i-j)*lambda_i*lambda_j)/(t*(1-t)) >= 0. Writing the curve as P_0+sum((P_(k+1)-P_k)*S_k) and integrating the triangle inequality bounds its length by the control polygon. The same argument applies after dropping zero controls and flipping a common negative sign. Exactly collinear controls in endpoint order give the endpoint distance directly. Collinear backtracking is not discarded. The normalized basis and its positivity are described in Piller's rational-curve notes; the length enclosure follows from the argument above.

Squared distances, homogeneous quotients and accumulated bounds remain exact until directed binary64 rounding. Correctly rounded shared rational square roots avoid premature overflow or loss of tiny distances. Earlier bounds are retained when later rounding is less tight. A loose polygon that overflows does not reject a finite curve: its upper bound stays absent until refinement. An exact chord or accumulated lower bound beyond binary64 range is an error. Cancellation/arithmetic errors return no partial report. The shared exact fraction cap is 65536 bits after reduction; at most 2*maxSegments-1 panels are evaluated and only compact panel metadata is retained.

These are conservative geometric length certificates, not a speed-quadrature error estimate. They cover even a regular cubic whose length is exactly 2 but whose motion is compressed around t=0.5 beyond neighboring binary64 parameters. Very tight tolerances can require many subdivisions or return a limit; no claim of arbitrary precision or arc-length parameterization is made. programs/science/conic_length.bas composes length, adaptive geometry and a feed-time estimate for a 3D conic toolpath. Evidence when accepted: output/rational-length-2026-10-27/validation.json. NURBS/surfaces, composite continuity, arc-length parameterization and broader math/application/OS/hardware qualification remain open.

B-spline and NURBS curve foundations

The shared CPU Rust NativeBSplineBasis and NativeNurbs<N> types support degree 0..16 curves with up to 65536 controls in 2D or 3D. This is a knot-vector representation, distinct from interpolation through data points.

  • BSPLINE(degree,knots,points) constructs a polynomial curve with unit weights.
  • NURBS(degree,knots,points,weights[,mode$]) constructs a rational curve. Mode is "WEIGHTED" (Euclidean control points, default) or "HOMOGENEOUS" (numerator controls, allowing directions at infinity).
  • Both return freely editable {"NURBS1",degree,knots,coordinates,weights,mode$}.
  • NURBSPOINT(curve,t[,side$]) evaluates a point.
  • NURBSDERIV(curve,t[,order[,side$]]) uses order 1 by default; orders 0..3 refer to the original knot coordinate, not a normalized span.
  • NURBSBATCH(curve,parameters[,order[,side$]]) returns complete input-order values (default order 0), with at most 65536 queries.
  • BSPLINEBASIS(curve,t[,order[,side$]]) returns {firstControl,values}: at most degree+1 local polynomial basis values or derivatives, before rational weighting. The BASIC index is one based; native NativeSplineBasisValues.first_control is zero based.

With n controls and degree p, exactly n+p+1 knots are required, all finite and nondecreasing. Each multiplicity is at most p+1 and n>=p+1. The active interval is closed [knots[p],knots[n]] in zero-based notation, and must have positive width. Unclamped and nonuniform vectors are supported. No extrapolation, parameter wrapping or automatic knot snapping occurs. An unclamped endpoint generally does not equal the first/last control point. Degree zero represents piecewise constants.

Side is "AUTO" by default: right-hand span at interior knots, left-hand span at the final endpoint. "LEFT" and "RIGHT" explicitly choose the limit at a join, including derivatives. Requesting an exterior side at the first/last active endpoint is an error. Repeated knots can reduce continuity or create a discontinuity at multiplicity p+1; evaluating both sides makes this visible. This API does not silently smooth or join disconnected pieces.

Native construction is NativeBSplineBasis::new(degree,&knots) and NativeNurbs::new(degree,&knots,&points,&weights), with polynomial and from_homogeneous alternatives. Basis accessors expose degree, knots, control_count and interval. basis.evaluate(t,order,NativeKnotSide) returns the compact local basis report. Curve point and derivative use automatic sides; point_on and derivative_on take NativeKnotSide explicitly. evaluate_many(&parameters,order,side) is complete or returns an error.

Evaluation computes exact local Cox-de Boor derivative jets, retaining the original binary64 knot/control/weight data. It reuses the rational Bezier engine's exact quotient recurrence, then rounds each final component once. Extreme knot spans, weighted products and derivative cancellations do not overflow prematurely. Signed-zero coordinates are preserved when the basis is exactly one-hot in weighted mode. Rational derivatives may be nonzero above the polynomial degree. Shared exact fractions are capped at 65536 bits after reduction; exhaustion is an error, with no approximate fallback. See Shene's basis derivation for the polynomial recurrence and local-support construction.

Signed and zero weights are admitted except all-zero vectors. Admission is not whole-curve regularity certification: each query rejects its raw zero denominator, including removable 0/0 and zero-weight spans. A zero denominator elsewhere is not searched for by point/batch queries. A finite local polynomial basis can be queried even if the rational curve has a pole at that parameter. Nonfinite inputs, inconsistent dimensions, invalid orders/sides and unrepresentable final components return errors.

Native construction stores O(n) data; a query uses O(log n) span search, O(p^2*(order+1)) exact basis work and O(p*(order+1)) temporary storage. It does not scan unrelated controls. BASIC packets are revalidated on each call; use NURBSBATCH to amortize that cost. Cancellation is checked during admission, basis construction and output computation; no partial batch escapes.

programs/science/nurbs_path.bas demonstrates a closed 3D multi-span conic and checks the one-sided tangent join. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-curves-2026-10-27/validation.json. Knot insertion/refinement, global domain certification, NURBS adaptive sampling/length, surfaces, broader continuity workflows and inverse arc-length traversal remain open, along with general math/application/OS/hardware acceptance.

Exact NURBS whole-span domains

NURBSDOMAIN(curve[,maxRefinements]) calls NativeNurbs<N>::domain(NativeNurbsDomainOptions). It examines every nonempty knot span over its closed interval, using original knots and homogeneous data. At an internal join both incident polynomial spans are included, even when NURBSPOINT with "AUTO" selects only the right one. This is a traversal regularity check, not just a collection of point queries.

The BASIC report is: {"NDOMAIN1",{from,to},status$,refinements,finiteCounts,zeroSpanCount,spans}. Each span row is: {knotSpanIndex,{a,b},status$,refinements,{counts},roots}.

Indices refer to the original knot vector, one based in BASIC and zero based in NativeNurbsSpanDomain.span_index. Zero-width knot spans are skipped. Native NativeNurbsDomainReport fields are interval, status, refinements, finite_counts, zero_denominator_spans and spans. A native span has interval and domain: Option<NativeRationalDomainReport>.

For a nonidentically-zero denominator, counts and finiteCounts have the five entries {distinct,denominatorMultiplicity,removable,poles,poleMultiplicity}. They count span-root incidences, not unique global parameter values. A zero at a shared knot is counted once for each incident closed polynomial span; its multiplicity or removable/pole classification can differ by side. Each root row is {lo,hi,"EXACT"|"OPEN",counts} in the original knot coordinate. EXACT is a singleton represented root. OPEN excludes both bounds and contains exactly the stated root counts. Common factors are cancelled for pole classification only when shared by every numerator coordinate; raw denominator zeros remain invalid point queries.

A denominator identically zero over a span has "ZERO_DENOMINATOR" status, empty counts/roots and native domain=None. Its infinitely many undefined parameters are represented by the span, not a finite root count. zeroSpanCount counts these spans; finiteCounts sums only the other spans. This applies whether or not their numerator polynomials also vanish.

Top-level status is "REGULAR" only when all closed-span denominators are proved nonzero. Other statuses are "ISOLATED", "RESOLUTION_LIMIT", "REFINEMENT_LIMIT" and "UNDEFINED_SPANS". Undefined spans take precedence, then a refinement limit, then a resolution limit. Individual span reports retain the other details. ISOLATED means each finite root is exact or lies alone between adjacent binary64 values. Multiple roots sharing one adjacent gap give RESOLUTION_LIMIT. Every finite count and interval remains complete when refinement or coordinate resolution prevents further isolation.

The default global refinement budget is 256, with an allowed range 0..4096 and BASIC's usual integer conversion. Earlier spans consume the shared budget; later spans are still classified exactly and retain their enclosing intervals. Zero budget requests exact counts without interior refinement. Signed binary64 lattice bisection handles negative knots, subnormals and intervals crossing zero; both signed zeros have one canonical representation in reports. Affine mapping to each normalized span is performed exactly, never by rounded child packets.

The Rust backend uses exact homogeneous de Boor span polynomials and the same generic polynomial/Sturm classifier as rational Bezier domains. Strictly same-sign, nonzero local weights provide an immediate regularity proof from the nonnegative partition of unity. All-zero local weights identify an undefined span directly. Other cases retain exact coefficients through gcd, multiplicity and root counting.

Degree and control-count admission remain 0..16 and at most 65536 controls. One call has a 2,000,000-step polynomial/work budget and at most 65536 root interval records; exact fractions remain capped at 65536 bits after reduction. These resource limits, arithmetic failures and cancellation return errors, never a partial clean report. Work limits do not silently skip later spans. Native report storage is bounded by the number of nonempty spans and root records. The result establishes denominator regularity only: it does not certify continuity across joins, finite binary64 point/derivative outputs, self-intersection freedom or machining clearance.

programs/science/nurbs_domain.bas guards a closed path and detects a pole introduced by editing its weight. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-domain-2026-10-27/validation.json. NURBS knot refinement, adaptive sampling/length, surfaces, continuity and inverse arc-length workflows, and broader math/application/OS/hardware acceptance remain separate open tasks.

NURBS knot refinement

NURBSREFINE(curve,insertedKnots[,mode$]) inserts an unordered multiset of finite knots within the closed active interval. It returns: {"NREFINE1",refinedCurve,status$,insertedCount,roundedControls,{errorBound}}. Use the second entry as an ordinary freely editable NURBS1 curve. Mode defaults to the input mode; explicit "WEIGHTED" or "HOMOGENEOUS" also permits representation conversion with an empty insertion list.

The Rust API is NativeNurbs<N>::refine(&[f64]) or refine_as(&[f64],homogeneous:bool), returning NativeNurbsRefinementReport<N> with curve, inserted, rounded_controls, homogeneous_error_bound and status:NativeNurbsRefinementStatus.

Exact homogeneous Boehm insertion preserves the original curve over the same closed active domain, including both sides of internal joins and nonclamped endpoints. Sorting makes insertion order deterministic. Each final multiplicity must be at most degree+1; this includes existing occurrences. Degree zero and full multiplicity are supported. Exterior knots and overfull multiplicities are rejected. No extrapolation, periodic wrapping or automatic knot removal occurs.

Working numerator/weight coefficients remain exact throughout the entire batch. A streaming buffer retains at most degree+2 controls, so repeated insertions do not repeatedly copy the full curve. Output coefficients are converted only after their last use. Unmodified controls keep their original bits when retaining the mode; an empty same-mode request is a bit-preserving copy.

"EXACT" means every represented output homogeneous coefficient equals its ideal exact refinement coefficient. For weighted output the represented numerator is the exact product of its binary64 point and weight. "ROUNDED" means at least one coefficient differs; roundedControls counts affected controls. The optional error bound is an upward-rounded maximum absolute error over all numerator and weight coefficients. Nonnegative partition-of-unity basis functions also bound each homogeneous VALUE error by this maximum on each active closed span. An empty bound means this maximum exceeds binary64 range. It is not a geometric distance, derivative bound or validity certificate: division near zero weight can amplify errors arbitrarily. Recheck the returned curve with NURBSDOMAIN before domain-sensitive use.

Weighted output cannot represent a zero-weight control with a nonzero homogeneous numerator (a direction at infinity); request homogeneous output. A zero numerator and zero weight is representable with zero Euclidean coordinates. Nonzero weights that round to zero and overflowing returned components are errors. Homogeneous output can overflow even when a weighted representation fits; select the representation explicitly when needed. No partial curve escapes on admission, arithmetic, work or cancellation errors.

Limits remain degree 0..16 and 65536 final controls. The call uses an 8,000,000-step work cap and the shared 65536-bit reduced-fraction cap. Sorting is O(m log m), span lookup O(m log n), knot merging/output O(n+m), and local coefficient work O(m*degree*dimension), excluding bounded big-integer arithmetic; working exact control storage is O(degree*dimension), with O(n+m) output storage. programs/science/nurbs_refinement.bas refines a closed exact circular path and checks its output through the same native-backed BASIC APIs. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-refinement-2026-10-27/validation.json. Adaptive NURBS sampling/length, surfaces, continuity/arc-length workflows and general math/application/OS/hardware qualification remain open.

Certified adaptive NURBS pieces

NURBSADAPT(curve[,tolerance[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]]]) samples every nonempty closed active knot span. Defaults are 1e-3, 4096 and 40. It returns {"NSAMPLE1",status$,segments,{maximumDeviation},pieces}. Each piece is {knotSpanIndex,{from,to},parameters,points,{maximumDeviation},status$}. Draw each piece separately. Even a continuous join retains two incident endpoints; a discontinuous join never adds a fabricated connecting segment. Original knot indices are one based in BASIC and zero based in Rust.

Native NativeNurbs<N>::sample(NativeCurveSamplingOptions) returns NativeNurbsSamples<N> with pieces, segments, maximum_deviation and status. Each NativeNurbsSamplePiece<N> has span_index, interval and samples:NativeCurveSamples<N>. Piece parameters increase strictly and include both closed-span endpoints. Sampling uses exact original homogeneous span polynomials and exact Bernstein restrictions, never rounded refinement packets.

The deviation certificate bounds Euclidean distance from every point of the original exact curve to its corresponding rounded output chord. Positive/common- sign rational control hulls and exact projection give upward-rounded L1 bounds, shared with rational Bezier sampling. Zero-weight/zero-numerator controls may be omitted; mixed signs or a zero-weight direction may require subdivision before a finite hull certificate exists. An empty bound means no finite certificate. This is geometric distance, not same-parameter, tangent, length or inverse- distance error. Repeated traversal can lie on a chord without increasing this error; use a length operation for travel distance.

Only CONVERGED meets tolerance. SEGMENT_LIMIT and RESOLUTION_LIMIT retain complete ordered output for every span, with honest per-piece/global bounds. Blocked panels remain in the result while other refinable panels continue. The global status prioritizes an unmet segment budget over blocked depth/float resolution, and otherwise converges only when every piece meets tolerance. Limits are global: maxSegments must be 1..65536 and at least the number of nonempty spans. An insufficient initial budget is an error, not a partial path. The output has at most segments+pieces points (131072 overall).

Finite tolerance must be positive. Depth is 1..2100; the larger cap covers the full signed finite knot range down to subnormal spacings. Midpoints are formed exactly before one final binary64 rounding, avoiding subtraction overflow. Adjacent parameter values and depth limits cannot imply convergence by themselves.

Whole-span exact domain validation precedes output: raw zeros (even removable), hidden one-sided poles and entirely undefined spans are errors. Domain analysis keeps its 2,000,000-step cap. Sampling then has a separate 16,000,000-step budget, the shared 65536-bit reduced-fraction cap, and at most one cached exact span. Heap/output storage is O(maxSegments+spans), not an exact-coefficient cache for every panel. Work/arithmetic/cancellation errors return no partial report. A regular denominator does not guarantee finite point outputs; output overflow also returns an error. Curve degree remains 0..16 and controls at most 65536.

programs/science/nurbs_sampling.bas checks a circular path and a disconnected piecewise path through the BASIC interface. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-sampling-2026-10-27/validation.json. Rational surfaces, continuity/arc-length workflows and broad math/application/OS/hardware qualification remain open.

Certified NURBS path length

NURBSLENGTH(curve[,absoluteTolerance[,relativeTolerance[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]]]]) returns {value,{absoluteError},lowerBound,{upperBound},segments,status$}. Defaults are 1e-6,1e-6,4096,1074. Native Rust uses NativeNurbs::<2/3>::length(NativeCurveLengthOptions) and the shared NativeCurveLengthReport / NativeCurveLengthStatus types.

The result sums traversal length over every nonempty closed knot span. Repeated travel counts; jumps between disconnected pieces do not. Degree-zero pieces contribute zero. Each span uses its own endpoint continuations, including both sides of repeated knots. This is curve length, not the length of sampled chords, and does not depend on a rounded knot-refinement packet.

Exact original homogeneous span polynomials are restricted in Bernstein form. Outward-rounded endpoint norms give lower bounds; positive-weight rational control polygons give upper bounds. For arbitrary degree, the rational Bernstein basis has monotone cumulative weights, so total variation is bounded by that polygon. Ordered collinear controls reduce to endpoint distance; reversing controls do not. Exact aggregate sums and intersections of earlier valid bounds avoid losing certificates to floating-point addition or refinement roundoff. Signed/zero weights are supported: mixed-sign restricted hulls may initially have no finite upper certificate and refine until one becomes available.

CONVERGED means absoluteError <= MAX(absoluteTolerance,relativeTolerance*value), compared exactly. Both tolerances must be finite/nonnegative, at least one positive. SEGMENT_LIMIT and RESOLUTION_LIMIT retain complete path bounds, including unresolved spans. {} for upper bound/error means no finite upper certificate has been established; the reported value then equals the lower bound and is not a converged estimate. A blocked span does not prevent other spans from refining. Parameter means are exact before rounding, including intervals from -MAX to +MAX. Lack of a representable interior parameter can yield RESOLUTION_LIMIT even though an exact real curve has interior motion.

Global segment cap: 1..65536, at least one per nonempty span; an insufficient budget is an error rather than partial coverage. Depth cap: 1..2100 per original span. All existing degree/control limits apply. Exact domain preflight rejects every raw denominator zero (including removable 0/0 and endpoints) and undefined span. The separate domain work limit remains in force. Length adds a 16,000,000-step work cap and uses the existing 65,536-bit fraction limit, cancellation checks, a bounded panel heap and one cached exact span. Work/bit exhaustion, cancellation or certified lower-bound overflow returns an error without a partial report. A loose polygon upper bound that overflows is unknown, not evidence that the actual length overflows. Absolute point coordinates may be unrepresentable while a finite length remains certifiable.

programs/science/nurbs_length.bas checks a closed circular path and disconnected cutting segments with a feed-time calculation. Independent exact Cox span polynomials and high-precision integrals qualify the bounds, including limits, backtracking and extreme scales; native and exported consumers are also required. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-length-2026-10-27/validation.json. Inverse arc-length traversal, rational surfaces, composite continuity workflows and broad math/application/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.

Tensor-product B-spline and NURBS surfaces

The Rust NativeNurbsSurface<N> engine supports 2D/3D coordinates, independent U/V degrees 0..16, nonuniform/repeated/nonclamped knots and at most 65536 total controls. Degree zero and discontinuous patches are valid. BASIC constructors:

  • BSPLINESURFACE({uDegree,vDegree},uKnots,vKnots,points) uses unit weights.
  • NURBSSURFACE({uDegree,vDegree},uKnots,vKnots,points,weights[,mode$]) accepts "WEIGHTED" Euclidean points (default) or "HOMOGENEOUS" numerator controls.
  • Points are a rectangular U-row/V-column grid of coordinate lists; weights have the same U/V shape. Native arrays are flattened U-major/V-fast: index=u*vCount+v. Each knot vector determines its axis control count.
  • The freely editable packet is {"NSURFACE1",{uDegree,vDegree},uKnots,vKnots,points,weights,mode$}.

NURBSSURFACEPOINT(S,u,v[,uSide$[,vSide$]]) returns a coordinate list. NURBSSURFACEDERIV(S,u,v,uOrder,vOrder[,uSide$[,vSide$]]) returns a mixed partial, with orders independently 0..3 (including (3,3)). NURBSSURFACEBATCH(S,{{u,v},...}[,uOrder[,vOrder[,uSide$[,vSide$]]]]) returns complete input-order results; both derivative orders default to zero. Each side defaults to "AUTO": the right continuation at interior knots, the left continuation at the final active endpoint. "LEFT"/"RIGHT" apply independently to U and V. A side pointing outside an active domain is an error; no extrapolation or snapping occurs. Endpoint continuations are computed from the selected nonempty knot spans.

Native constructors are new([p,q],[&uKnots,&vKnots],&points,&weights), from_homogeneous(...) and polynomial([p,q],[&uKnots,&vKnots],&points). Accessors expose bases(), shape(), coordinates(), weights() and is_homogeneous(). Queries are point([u,v]), point_on([u,v],[uSide,vSide]), derivative([u,v],[du,dv]), derivative_on([u,v],[du,dv],[uSide,vSide]) and evaluate_many(&parameters,[du,dv],[uSide,vSide]). Sides use NativeKnotSide.

The backend reuses exact local Cox-de Boor basis jets. Numerator/denominator products, mixed quotient differentiation and original-knot scaling stay exact until each final component rounds once to binary64. Rational derivatives can remain nonzero above the polynomial degree. Zero/signed weights are admitted except an all-zero weight array; every query rejects a raw zero denominator, including removable 0/0. Homogeneous input permits directions at infinity in the control net. Weighted one-hot queries preserve the original control's signed zeros after the denominator check.

Inputs, outputs and knots must be finite. Shape, degree, total control, query and derivative limits are checked. Batches contain at most 65536 parameter pairs and preflight all parameter domains before computing results. A shared 16,000,000 charged-step budget covers a complete query/batch, including local basis and mixed-jet work; each query does not receive a fresh batch budget. The existing reduced-fraction 65536-bit cap and cancellation checks also apply. Exhaustion, cancellation, a zero denominator or final overflow returns an error without partial output. A BASIC query revalidates the entire editable packet; batching amortizes that cost. Native queries use only the local (uDegree+1)*(vDegree+1) control neighborhood after construction.

This is a pointwise surface foundation, with exact original-data derivative evaluation. It does not certify a whole patch free of denominator zeros or provide tessellation error bounds, trimming/intersections, area integration or a complete CAD system. Those and inverse arc-length traversal remain open. programs/science/nurbs_surface.bas exercises a rational cylinder and its tangents. Required qualification includes exact independent polynomial/series references, SciPy comparisons where supported, analytic sphere/cylinder models, large grids, cancellation, BASIC recovery and standalone export. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-surface-2026-10-27/validation.json. Broader math/application/OS/image/architecture/hardware gates remain open.

Whole-patch NURBS surface denominator certificates

NURBSSURFACEDOMAIN(surface[,maxCells[,maxDepth]]) examines every nonempty closed U/V knot rectangle, with separate one-sided continuations at joins. It returns {"NSDOMAIN1",{{uFrom,uTo},{vFrom,vTo}},status$,patches,refinements,zeroCells,unresolvedCells,cells}. Each cell is {{uSpan,vSpan},{{u0,u1},{v0,v1}},status$,{lowerW,upperW},witnesses}. Span indices are one-based in BASIC and zero-based in Rust. Cells are ordered by original patch and rectangle coordinates. They cover every patch completely; shared edges are included on both sides.

Native Rust uses NativeNurbsSurface::domain(NativeNurbsSurfaceDomainOptions) and typed NativeNurbsSurfaceDomainReport / NativeNurbsSurfaceDomainCell records. Report/cell status types are NativeNurbsSurfaceDomainStatus and NativeNurbsSurfaceDomainCellStatus. Defaults are 4096 total cells and depth 40 per axis. Limits: cells 1..65536 and depth 1..2100. At least one cell per original knot rectangle is required; insufficient initial coverage is an error.

Cell meanings:

  • POSITIVE / NEGATIVE certify a strictly nonzero denominator throughout the closed cell, including real parameter pairs between binary64 values.
  • IDENTICALLY_ZERO certifies the denominator is zero everywhere in the cell.
  • ZERO_WITNESS provides one parameter pair with an exact raw denominator zero.
  • SIGN_CHANGE provides two parameter pairs with exact opposite denominator signs; continuity within that patch proves at least one zero between them.
  • CELL_LIMIT / RESOLUTION_LIMIT mean unresolved. They never mean regular. Resolution covers per-axis depth or a lack of an interior binary64 midpoint. Parameter-independent directions are not pointlessly subdivided.

Witnesses belong to the cell's selected patch continuation, which can differ from an automatic point query at a discontinuous join. Identically-zero and regular/limited cells have no witness list. A cell containing proved zeros is not subdivided further just to locate every zero. zeroCells counts cell incidences, not distinct zeros, poles or connected zero-set components. Raw removable zeros are included. unresolvedCells is reported even when zeros have also been proved elsewhere.

Overall status is REGULAR only if every cell is Positive/Negative; ZERO_DENOMINATOR if any cell proves a zero; otherwise CELL_LIMIT takes precedence over RESOLUTION_LIMIT. A finite sampled grid alone never admits a patch as regular. Different signs in disconnected patch continuations do not imply a zero between those patches.

The shared Rust exact de Boor channel kernel produces original-data tensor power coefficients, converted exactly to Bernstein controls. All restrictions use that original net; no rounded child surface is used. Convex control bounds are rounded outwards for lowerW/upperW. Strict same-sign original weights provide an inexpensive valid certificate. For a nonnegative Bernstein net whose corners are positive, the closed-cell lower bound also uses minCorner * 2^(-max(uDegree-1,0)-max(vDegree-1,0)). This follows from the minimum of the endpoint Bernstein basis sums; degree-zero axes contribute one. Negative nets use the same argument after a sign flip. Thus interior zero controls do not prevent a valid strict certificate. A strict lower bound can round to zero at extreme scales; the Positive/Negative status comes from the exact proof, not the rounded bound alone.

Subdivision has one global cell budget, breadth-first fairness, separate per-axis depths, overflow-safe exact midpoints and one cached exact patch. The domain operation has a 16,000,000 charged-step limit and the existing 65536-bit reduced-fraction cap. Work/bit exhaustion or cancellation is an error without a partial report. Cell/depth/parameter limits instead retain complete coverage and explicitly unresolved cells.

This certifies denominator regularity only. It does not establish finite coordinate outputs, geometric continuity, injectivity, tessellation accuracy, surface area, or complete algebraic classification of a bivariate zero set. Tangent zeros at nonrepresentable parameters can remain unresolved. Those limits, trimming/intersections, area, inverse arc-length traversal and broader math/application/OS/image/hardware gates remain explicit follow-on work. programs/science/nurbs_surface_domain.bas admits a regular cylinder and rejects a hidden tangent-zero patch before tessellation. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-surface-domain-2026-10-27/validation.json.

Certified NURBS surface meshes

NativeNurbsSurface<N>::tessellate(NativeNurbsSurfaceMeshOptions) is the CPU native counterpart of NURBSSURFACEMESH. Options contain absolute_tolerance (default 1e-3), max_triangles (8192) and max_depth (40). NativeNurbsSurfaceMesh<N> contains interval, triangles, maximum_deviation: Option<f64>, status and pieces. Status is NativeNurbsSurfaceMeshStatus::{Converged,TriangleLimit,ResolutionLimit}.

Each NativeNurbsSurfaceMeshPiece<N> contains original zero-based spans, interval, parameters: [Vec<f64>;2], U-major/V-fast vertices, local zero-based triangles, optional cell_deviation bounds for pairs of triangles, and maximum_deviation. Grids conform in parameter space across the complete surface; patch seams retain independent indices and one-sided coordinates. Degenerate geometric triangles retain their parameter coverage. The certificate bounds same-parameter positional error against actual rounded vertices; it does not certify normals, injectivity, a closed solid or seam welding.

See GEOMETRY.md for the exact proof, output ordering, admission and all limits. Raw-denominator admission and meshing share one bounded operation; cancellation or hard arithmetic/work/coordinate failures return no partial mesh. A TriangleLimit/ResolutionLimit report still covers all original patches, but must not be treated as satisfying the requested tolerance. None is an unknown finite upper bound, never zero. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-surface-mesh-2026-10-27/validation.json.

Indexed NURBS surface consumers

NativeNurbsSurface<3>::indexed_mesh(NativeNurbsIndexedMeshOptions) returns an immutable NativeNurbsIndexedMesh. Options contain mesh: NativeNurbsSurfaceMeshOptions, seam_policy: NativeNurbsSeamPolicy::{Continuous,Separate} (default Continuous), and explicit wrap_axes: [bool;2] (default false/false). The triangle budget is capped at 100000 for compatibility with NativeTriangleMesh3.

Accessors: mesh(), maximum_deviation(), patches(), source_vertices(), joined_seams(), unjoined_seams(), wrap_axes() and patch_vertex_indices(). Native mesh faces/maps use zero-based indices. into_mesh(self) consumes the result and returns the shared mesh. The private fields prevent editing geometry while retaining a trusted certificate. Cloning the result preserves the same immutable semantics.

Indexing requires converged tessellation and joins only proven identical original rational boundaries. Wrapped boundaries must agree with the same parameter orientation; internal nonidentical boundaries remain separate. No global coordinate/epsilon welding occurs. See GEOMETRY.md for the exact proof, packet correspondence, resource limits and failure behavior. NativeSolidDomain3 and NativeStl consume result.mesh() directly. Topology validity, embedded solidity and format precision remain independent checks; positional accuracy does not certify these properties. Evidence when accepted: output/nurbs-indexed-mesh-2026-10-27/validation.json.

## Rational Bezier curves and conics

`RBEZIER(coordinates,weights[,mode])` creates an editable
`{"RBEZIER1",coordinates,weights,mode}` packet. The shared Rust type is
`NativeRationalBezier<2>` or `NativeRationalBezier<3>`, with two to four
controls (degree one through three). Modes are case-insensitive:

- `"WEIGHTED"` (default): coordinates are Euclidean control points. The numerator
  controls are the exact products of those coordinates and their weights.
  Native construction is `NativeRationalBezier::new(points,weights)`.
- `"HOMOGENEOUS"`: coordinates already are numerator controls; they are not
  multiplied by weights. A nonzero numerator with zero weight represents a
  control direction at infinity. Native construction is
  `NativeRationalBezier::from_homogeneous(numerators,weights)`.

All coordinate/weight inputs must be finite, with one weight per control and at
least one nonzero weight. Zero and negative weights are supported. These two
representations are intentionally distinct: a zero weight removes a weighted
Euclidean control's contribution, while a homogeneous zero-weight numerator
can contribute a direction at infinity.

| BASIC operation | Shared native operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RBEZIERPOINT(curve,t)` | `point(t)` | Two-/three-component point |
| `RBEZIERDERIV(curve,t[,order])` | `derivative(t,order)` | Original-parameter derivative; default order 1, supported 0–3 |
| `RBEZIERBATCH(curve,parameters[,order])` | `evaluate_many(parameters,order)` | Input-order rows; default order 0 |
| `RBEZIERSAMPLE(curve,segments)` | `sample_uniform(segments)` | `segments+1` point rows with uniform parameter spacing |
| `RBEZIERSPLIT(curve,t)` | `split(t)` | Two child curves with parameters mapping to `[0,t]` and `[t,1]` |

Native getters are `coordinates()`, `weights()`, `is_homogeneous()` and
`degree()`. Parameters must be finite and inside `[0,1]`. There is no implicit
extrapolation. Derivatives of a rational curve need not vanish above its
numerator degree. The common curve fraction core evaluates the represented
numerator and denominator exactly, forms quotient derivatives, and rounds only
the returned components. This avoids premature weight-product overflow and
rounded cancellation. Weighted endpoint points retain the original coordinates
verbatim when their denominator is nonzero.

The exact represented denominator must be nonzero at every queried parameter.
A zero denominator is an error, even for a removable `0/0`; no epsilon cutoff or
automatic limiting value is substituted. Signed weights can create poles and
unbounded portions. Successful point or batch queries do not certify that the
whole interval is pole-free. Uniform sampling is neither arc-length spacing nor
a geometric error bound, and joining samples across an unqueried pole is unsafe.
Positive weights provide the usual control-hull property in weighted mode.

Subdivision evaluates the homogeneous de Casteljau controls in exact arithmetic.
Each returned weight and coordinate is rounded once. A child uses weighted
coordinates where finite dehomogenization is possible, otherwise homogeneous
coordinates retain its infinite controls. Splitting returns an error if a
nonzero weight rounds to zero, all child weights vanish, or the chosen output
representation cannot be finite. No common rescaling rescue is attempted.
Subsequent queries use the rounded child data; repeated splitting can accumulate
error and perturb denominator roots. Child derivatives use their new local
parameters, so compare them with the parent's derivatives multiplied by the
appropriate parameter-scale power.

Batches accept at most 65,536 parameters. Uniform sampling accepts 1–65,536
segments. The shared 65,536-bit reduced numerator/denominator bound limits exact
arithmetic; intermediate temporaries can be larger. Traversals check
cancellation, and batch/subdivision errors return no partial result. Final
unrepresentable components raise `RealOverflow`. Editable BASIC packets require
no registration or backend version changes.

For example, `RBEZIER({{1,0},{0,1},{-1,0}},{1,0,1},"HOMOGENEOUS")` represents
the upper half of a unit circle without irrational input weights. The
`programs/science/rational_conic.bas` consumer scales this construction into a
3D CAD ellipse and checks its tangents and subdivision. Definitions follow the
[Michigan Tech rational curve notes](https://pages.mtu.edu/~shene/COURSES/cs3621/NOTES/curves/rational.html)
and the [homogeneous circular-arc construction](https://www.cs.sjsu.edu/faculty/pollett/216.1.10s/Lec09022010.html).
No external implementation or new dependency is incorporated.

Qualification: exact Bernstein-polynomial and independent symbolic derivative
references, conic identities, subdivision data, native/BASIC/export parity and
resource/cancellation checks in
`output/rational-bezier-2026-10-26/validation.json` when accepted.
NURBS/rational surfaces, composite/arc-length workflows and broader CAD,
math/application/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.

### Exact rational-curve interval checks

`RBEZIERDOMAIN(curve[,from,to[,maxRefinements]])` calls the shared Rust
`NativeRationalBezier::domain(from,to,NativeRationalDomainOptions)`.
The default closed interval is `[0,1]`; explicit bounds must be finite,
ordered and inside that interval. Subdivision budget defaults to 256 and
accepts 0–4096. Zero requests exact counts with any unresolved intervals retained.
BASIC applies its usual integer conversion to the budget (for example, 1.5
becomes 2); the native Rust option is an integer.

The result is freely readable BASIC data:

```text
{"RDOMAIN1",{from,to},status$,refinements,counts,{intervals...}}
counts = {distinct,denominatorMultiplicity,removable,poles,poleMultiplicity}
interval = {lower,upper,"EXACT"|"OPEN",counts}
```

All counts refer to exact polynomials formed from the represented input
coordinates and weights, including unrounded weighted products.
`distinct` counts denominator zeros; `denominatorMultiplicity` includes
repetition. A common polynomial GCD across **every** numerator and the denominator
identifies cancellations. `removable` counts zeros fully removed by cancellation;
`poles` counts the remaining distinct poles; `poleMultiplicity` sums their orders
after cancellation (the largest remaining order across coordinates).
A partially cancelled root remains a pole. Raw `0/0` is still undefined for
point/derivative queries, so only zero **denominator** roots establishes a usable
whole interval.

`EXACT` is a singleton exactly representable root. `OPEN` means roots lie
strictly between the bounds; roots at either bound are reported separately.
Reports cover the whole requested closed interval without duplicate endpoint
counts. The status is:

- `REGULAR`: no denominator zeros in the entire closed interval.
- `ISOLATED`: every root is an exact singleton or is alone between adjacent
  binary64 bounds. These are enclosures, not rounded root estimates.
- `RESOLUTION_LIMIT`: distinct roots share an adjacent-binary64 gap; exact
  counts and multiplicities are retained without claiming separate locations.
- `REFINEMENT_LIMIT`: the budget ended with at least one wider interval.
  Counts remain exact; some other intervals may also contain unresolved clusters.

Root counting reuses the algebra engine's exact Sturm kernel with one-sided
endpoint signs; multiplicities use repeated polynomial GCDs. The algebra
certificate checker retains independent multiplication-identity verification.
Curve coefficients retain the 65,536-bit reduced fraction bound; symbolic
coefficients retain their existing 4,096-bit and charged-work policies.
Domain checks additionally cap polynomial work at 2,000,000 charged steps.
Cancellation or arithmetic/work exhaustion raises an error with no partial report.
Binary64 bit-range subdivision bounds refinement even near subnormal parameters.

`REGULAR` certifies denominator absence only: it does not certify finite
rounded coordinates, safe derivative magnitudes, geometric accuracy, or
regular nonzero tangents. Edited or rounded subdivided curves must be checked
again. NURBS, surfaces and composite
arc-length workflows remain open.

`programs/science/rational_domain.bas` demonstrates a pole missed by uniform
sampling and a checked conic. Qualification uses independent exact SymPy
polynomials, GCDs and interval counts
([SymPy polynomial reference](https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/polys/reference.html)),
native/BASIC/export parity and resource/recovery checks. Evidence:
`output/rational-domain-2026-10-27/validation.json` when accepted.

### Adaptive rational-curve polylines

`RBEZIERADAPT(curve,tolerance[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]])` calls
`NativeRationalBezier::sample(NativeCurveSamplingOptions)` and returns:

```text
{parameters,points,{maximumDeviation},status$}
```

The default limits are 4096 segments and depth 40. Rational sampling accepts
1–65,536 segments and depth 1–1074; the existing polynomial sampler retains its
own depth limit of 52. BASIC uses its usual integer conversion for the limits.
Tolerance must be positive and finite. Parameters cover `[0,1]` in increasing
order, with one more point than segments. Each point is the same correctly
rounded original-curve query returned by `RBEZIERPOINT`.

The finite deviation bounds the Euclidean distance from **every exact curve
point in each parameter interval to its corresponding rounded output segment**.
It is a geometric, one-sided bound. It does not bound same-parameter linear
interpolation, tangent error, arc-length spacing, or the reverse distance from
the segment to the curve. Nonlinear rational parameterizations of straight
segments may therefore have a zero geometric bound.

The Rust implementation first performs an exact whole-interval denominator
check. Any denominator zero, including removable `0/0` and endpoint zeros,
raises an error before a polyline is returned. It then computes exact homogeneous
Bernstein controls restricted from the original curve to each candidate
interval. These are scratch values, not rounded child packets. If their
nonzero weights have one sign, the curve is a convex combination of their
dehomogenized controls. A zero weight with all-zero numerators contributes
nothing; a zero weight with a nonzero numerator has no finite hull bound yet.

For each finite exact control, Rust projects onto the actual rounded output
segment and computes an exact L1 residual. The largest residual conservatively
bounds Euclidean distance over the whole convex hull, including endpoint
rounding. The reported value rounds upward once. This also handles coincident
endpoints and collinear backtracking without mistaking an infinite line for a
finite segment. Mixed-sign controls or directions at infinity trigger
refinement until a finite bound is established or a limit is reached.
The [nonnegative-weight convex-hull property](https://pages.mtu.edu/~shene/COURSES/cs3621/NOTES/spline/NURBS/NURBS-property.html)
supplies the geometric basis; common negative weight scales are equivalent.

`CONVERGED` means every segment's bound is at most the requested tolerance.
`SEGMENT_LIMIT` and `RESOLUTION_LIMIT` retain a complete ordered polyline;
the latter covers the requested depth or an unavailable distinct binary64
midpoint. Inspect the status before treating the tolerance as achieved.
`{maximumDeviation}` is empty if no finite bound was established, including
unresolved control weights or bound overflow. Limits return an estimate to
inspect, not permission to claim accuracy.

The heap stores finite panel metadata and points, not a growing tree of exact
controls. At most `2*maxSegments-1` panels are evaluated; exact scratch arithmetic
retains the shared 65,536-bit reduced fraction limit. Cancellation is checked
during refinement and homogeneous restriction. Arithmetic/work failure or an
unrepresentable sampled coordinate raises an error with no partial result.
A finite geometric certificate does not promise finite derivatives or regular
tangents. Subnormal geometry and bounds may hit the final point-rounding floor.

Qualification includes independent exact change-of-variable Bernstein
certificates, dense exact point-to-segment comparisons, compressed-parameter
curves, homogeneous underflow, native resources/cancellation and interpreted/
exported BASIC parity. Consumer: `programs/science/adaptive_conic.bas`.
Evidence: `output/rational-sampling-2026-10-27/validation.json` when accepted.
NURBS/surfaces, composite continuity and arc-length
parameterization, and broader application/OS/hardware acceptance remain open.


### Certified rational-curve length

`RBEZIERLENGTH(curve[,absTol[,relTol[,maxSegments[,maxDepth]]]])` calls
`NativeRationalBezier<N>::length(NativeCurveLengthOptions)` for the complete
2D/3D linear, quadratic or cubic curve on [0,1]. It returns:

`{value,{absoluteError},lowerBound,{upperBound},segments,status$}`

Native fields have the corresponding snake_case names in
`NativeCurveLengthReport`. Optional numbers are empty lists/`None` when no
finite upper certificate has been established; then `value=lowerBound` and
there is no accuracy claim. `NativeCurveLengthStatus` is `CONVERGED`,
`SEGMENT_LIMIT` or `RESOLUTION_LIMIT`. Both bounds cover the **whole path**,
including repeated traversal, even on a limit. The estimate is the rounded
midpoint of a finite enclosure; `absoluteError` bounds its distance to either
end. Only `CONVERGED` meets
`absoluteError <= max(absTol,relTol*abs(value))`, compared without floating
overflow/underflow.

Defaults are absolute and relative tolerances `1e-6`, 4096 segments and depth
1074. Tolerances must be finite/nonnegative with at least one positive;
segments are 1..65536 and depth is 1..1074. BASIC integer options use the
language's usual integer conversion. A supplied absolute tolerance alone
leaves the default relative tolerance enabled; pass zero explicitly to
disable it. Depth exhaustion or no interior binary64 midpoint reports
`RESOLUTION_LIMIT`. Limits do not report success or silently omit intervals.

The engine first rejects every exact raw denominator zero on [0,1], including
removable and endpoint zeros. Each panel restricts the **original exact
homogeneous data**, with the same bounded Rust arithmetic used by sampling.
For a finite same-sign control polygon, endpoint distance is a lower bound
and control-polygon length is an upper bound. Mixed signs or a nonzero
direction at infinity require refinement before providing that upper bound.
Zero homogeneous controls contribute nothing.

Why the upper bound is valid: for normalized positive rational Bernstein
weights `lambda_i`, put `S_k=sum(i>k,lambda_i)`. Then
`S'_k=sum(j<=k<i,(i-j)*lambda_i*lambda_j)/(t*(1-t)) >= 0`.
Writing the curve as `P_0+sum((P_(k+1)-P_k)*S_k)` and integrating the triangle
inequality bounds its length by the control polygon. The same argument
applies after dropping zero controls and flipping a common negative sign.
Exactly collinear controls in endpoint order give the endpoint distance
directly. Collinear backtracking is **not** discarded. The normalized basis
and its positivity are described in
[Piller's rational-curve notes](https://web.uni-miskolc.hu/~matip/geometric_en/pages/05_Racional.html);
the length enclosure follows from the argument above.

Squared distances, homogeneous quotients and accumulated bounds remain exact
until directed binary64 rounding. Correctly rounded shared rational square
roots avoid premature overflow or loss of tiny distances. Earlier bounds are
retained when later rounding is less tight. A loose polygon that overflows
does not reject a finite curve: its upper bound stays absent until refinement.
An exact chord or accumulated lower bound beyond binary64 range is an error.
Cancellation/arithmetic errors return no partial report. The shared exact
fraction cap is 65536 bits after reduction; at most `2*maxSegments-1` panels
are evaluated and only compact panel metadata is retained.

These are conservative geometric length certificates, not a speed-quadrature
error estimate. They cover even a regular cubic whose length is exactly 2
but whose motion is compressed around t=0.5 beyond neighboring binary64
parameters. Very tight tolerances can require many subdivisions or return a
limit; no claim of arbitrary precision or arc-length parameterization is made.
`programs/science/conic_length.bas` composes length, adaptive geometry and a
feed-time estimate for a 3D conic toolpath. Evidence when accepted:
`output/rational-length-2026-10-27/validation.json`.
NURBS/surfaces, composite continuity, arc-length parameterization and broader
math/application/OS/hardware qualification remain open.


### B-spline and NURBS curve foundations

The shared CPU Rust `NativeBSplineBasis` and `NativeNurbs<N>` types support
degree 0..16 curves with up to 65536 controls in 2D or 3D. This is a knot-vector
representation, distinct from interpolation through data points.

- `BSPLINE(degree,knots,points)` constructs a polynomial curve with unit weights.
- `NURBS(degree,knots,points,weights[,mode$])` constructs a rational curve.
  Mode is `"WEIGHTED"` (Euclidean control points, default) or `"HOMOGENEOUS"`
  (numerator controls, allowing directions at infinity).
- Both return freely editable `{"NURBS1",degree,knots,coordinates,weights,mode$}`.
- `NURBSPOINT(curve,t[,side$])` evaluates a point.
- `NURBSDERIV(curve,t[,order[,side$]])` uses order 1 by default; orders 0..3
  refer to the **original knot coordinate**, not a normalized span.
- `NURBSBATCH(curve,parameters[,order[,side$]])` returns complete input-order
  values (default order 0), with at most 65536 queries.
- `BSPLINEBASIS(curve,t[,order[,side$]])` returns `{firstControl,values}`:
  at most degree+1 local **polynomial** basis values or derivatives, before
  rational weighting. The BASIC index is one based; native
  `NativeSplineBasisValues.first_control` is zero based.

With `n` controls and degree `p`, exactly `n+p+1` knots are required, all
finite and nondecreasing. Each multiplicity is at most `p+1` and `n>=p+1`.
The active interval is closed `[knots[p],knots[n]]` in zero-based notation,
and must have positive width. Unclamped and nonuniform vectors are supported.
No extrapolation, parameter wrapping or automatic knot snapping occurs.
An unclamped endpoint generally does not equal the first/last control point.
Degree zero represents piecewise constants.

Side is `"AUTO"` by default: right-hand span at interior knots, left-hand span
at the final endpoint. `"LEFT"` and `"RIGHT"` explicitly choose the limit at
a join, including derivatives. Requesting an exterior side at the first/last
active endpoint is an error. Repeated knots can reduce continuity or create
a discontinuity at multiplicity `p+1`; evaluating both sides makes this visible.
This API does not silently smooth or join disconnected pieces.

Native construction is `NativeBSplineBasis::new(degree,&knots)` and
`NativeNurbs::new(degree,&knots,&points,&weights)`, with `polynomial` and
`from_homogeneous` alternatives. Basis accessors expose `degree`, `knots`,
`control_count` and `interval`. `basis.evaluate(t,order,NativeKnotSide)`
returns the compact local basis report. Curve `point` and `derivative` use
automatic sides; `point_on` and `derivative_on` take `NativeKnotSide` explicitly.
`evaluate_many(&parameters,order,side)` is complete or returns an error.

Evaluation computes exact local Cox-de Boor derivative jets, retaining the
original binary64 knot/control/weight data. It reuses the rational Bezier
engine's exact quotient recurrence, then rounds each final component once.
Extreme knot spans, weighted products and derivative cancellations do not
overflow prematurely. Signed-zero coordinates are preserved when the basis
is exactly one-hot in weighted mode. Rational derivatives may be nonzero
above the polynomial degree. Shared exact fractions are capped at 65536 bits
after reduction; exhaustion is an error, with no approximate fallback.
See [Shene's basis derivation](https://pages.mtu.edu/~shene/COURSES/cs3621/NOTES/spline/bspline-basis.html)
for the polynomial recurrence and local-support construction.

Signed and zero weights are admitted except all-zero vectors. Admission is
**not** whole-curve regularity certification: each query rejects its raw zero
denominator, including removable 0/0 and zero-weight spans. A zero denominator
elsewhere is not searched for by point/batch queries. A finite local polynomial
basis can be queried even if the rational curve has a pole at that parameter.
Nonfinite inputs, inconsistent dimensions, invalid orders/sides and
unrepresentable final components return errors.

Native construction stores O(n) data; a query uses O(log n) span search,
O(p^2*(order+1)) exact basis work and O(p*(order+1)) temporary storage.
It does not scan unrelated controls. BASIC packets are revalidated on each
call; use `NURBSBATCH` to amortize that cost. Cancellation is checked during
admission, basis construction and output computation; no partial batch escapes.

`programs/science/nurbs_path.bas` demonstrates a closed 3D multi-span conic and
checks the one-sided tangent join. Evidence when accepted:
`output/nurbs-curves-2026-10-27/validation.json`. Knot insertion/refinement,
global domain certification, NURBS adaptive sampling/length, surfaces, broader
continuity workflows and inverse arc-length traversal remain open, along with
general math/application/OS/hardware acceptance.


### Exact NURBS whole-span domains

`NURBSDOMAIN(curve[,maxRefinements])` calls
`NativeNurbs<N>::domain(NativeNurbsDomainOptions)`. It examines **every nonempty
knot span over its closed interval**, using original knots and homogeneous
data. At an internal join both incident polynomial spans are included, even
when `NURBSPOINT` with `"AUTO"` selects only the right one. This is a traversal
regularity check, not just a collection of point queries.

The BASIC report is:
`{"NDOMAIN1",{from,to},status$,refinements,finiteCounts,zeroSpanCount,spans}`.
Each span row is:
`{knotSpanIndex,{a,b},status$,refinements,{counts},roots}`.

Indices refer to the original knot vector, one based in BASIC and zero based
in `NativeNurbsSpanDomain.span_index`. Zero-width knot spans are skipped.
Native `NativeNurbsDomainReport` fields are `interval`, `status`,
`refinements`, `finite_counts`, `zero_denominator_spans` and `spans`.
A native span has `interval` and `domain: Option<NativeRationalDomainReport>`.

For a nonidentically-zero denominator, `counts` and `finiteCounts` have the
five entries `{distinct,denominatorMultiplicity,removable,poles,poleMultiplicity}`.
They count **span-root incidences**, not unique global parameter values.
A zero at a shared knot is counted once for each incident closed polynomial
span; its multiplicity or removable/pole classification can differ by side.
Each root row is `{lo,hi,"EXACT"|"OPEN",counts}` in the **original knot
coordinate**. `EXACT` is a singleton represented root. `OPEN` excludes both
bounds and contains exactly the stated root counts. Common factors are
cancelled for pole classification only when shared by every numerator
coordinate; raw denominator zeros remain invalid point queries.

A denominator identically zero over a span has `"ZERO_DENOMINATOR"` status,
empty `counts`/`roots` and native `domain=None`. Its infinitely many undefined
parameters are represented by the span, **not** a finite root count.
`zeroSpanCount` counts these spans; `finiteCounts` sums only the other spans.
This applies whether or not their numerator polynomials also vanish.

Top-level status is `"REGULAR"` only when all closed-span denominators are
proved nonzero. Other statuses are `"ISOLATED"`, `"RESOLUTION_LIMIT"`,
`"REFINEMENT_LIMIT"` and `"UNDEFINED_SPANS"`. Undefined spans take precedence,
then a refinement limit, then a resolution limit. Individual span reports
retain the other details. `ISOLATED` means each finite root is exact or lies
alone between adjacent binary64 values. Multiple roots sharing one adjacent
gap give `RESOLUTION_LIMIT`. Every finite count and interval remains complete
when refinement or coordinate resolution prevents further isolation.

The default global refinement budget is 256, with an allowed range 0..4096
and BASIC's usual integer conversion. Earlier spans consume the shared budget;
later spans are still classified exactly and retain their enclosing intervals.
Zero budget requests exact counts without interior refinement. Signed binary64
lattice bisection handles negative knots, subnormals and intervals crossing zero;
both signed zeros have one canonical representation in reports. Affine mapping
to each normalized span is performed exactly, never by rounded child packets.

The Rust backend uses exact homogeneous de Boor span polynomials and the same
generic polynomial/Sturm classifier as rational Bezier domains. Strictly
same-sign, nonzero local weights provide an immediate regularity proof from
the nonnegative partition of unity. All-zero local weights identify an
undefined span directly. Other cases retain exact coefficients through gcd,
multiplicity and root counting.

Degree and control-count admission remain 0..16 and at most 65536 controls.
One call has a 2,000,000-step polynomial/work budget and at most 65536 root
interval records; exact fractions remain capped at 65536 bits after reduction.
These resource limits, arithmetic failures and cancellation return errors,
never a partial clean report. Work limits do not silently skip later spans.
Native report storage is bounded by the number of nonempty spans and root
records. The result establishes denominator regularity only: it does not
certify continuity across joins, finite binary64 point/derivative outputs,
self-intersection freedom or machining clearance.

`output/nurbs-domain-2026-10-27/validation.json`.

### NURBS knot refinement

`NURBSREFINE(curve,insertedKnots[,mode$])` inserts an unordered multiset of
finite knots within the closed active interval. It returns:
`{"NREFINE1",refinedCurve,status$,insertedCount,roundedControls,{errorBound}}`.
Use the second entry as an ordinary freely editable `NURBS1` curve.
Mode defaults to the input mode; explicit `"WEIGHTED"` or `"HOMOGENEOUS"`
also permits representation conversion with an empty insertion list.

The Rust API is `NativeNurbs<N>::refine(&[f64])` or
`refine_as(&[f64],homogeneous:bool)`, returning
`NativeNurbsRefinementReport<N>` with `curve`, `inserted`, `rounded_controls`,
`homogeneous_error_bound` and `status:NativeNurbsRefinementStatus`.

Exact homogeneous Boehm insertion preserves the original curve over the same
closed active domain, including both sides of internal joins and nonclamped
endpoints. Sorting makes insertion order deterministic. Each final multiplicity
must be at most degree+1; this includes existing occurrences. Degree zero and
full multiplicity are supported. Exterior knots and overfull multiplicities
are rejected. No extrapolation, periodic wrapping or automatic knot removal occurs.

Working numerator/weight coefficients remain exact throughout the entire
batch. A streaming buffer retains at most degree+2 controls, so repeated
insertions do not repeatedly copy the full curve. Output coefficients are
converted only after their last use. Unmodified controls keep their original
bits when retaining the mode; an empty same-mode request is a bit-preserving copy.

`"EXACT"` means every represented output homogeneous coefficient equals its
ideal exact refinement coefficient. For weighted output the represented
numerator is the exact product of its binary64 point and weight. `"ROUNDED"`
means at least one coefficient differs; `roundedControls` counts affected
controls. The optional error bound is an upward-rounded maximum absolute error
over all numerator and weight coefficients. Nonnegative partition-of-unity
basis functions also bound each homogeneous VALUE error by this maximum on
each active closed span. An empty bound means this maximum exceeds binary64
range. It is **not** a geometric distance, derivative bound or validity
certificate: division near zero weight can amplify errors arbitrarily.
Recheck the returned curve with `NURBSDOMAIN` before domain-sensitive use.

Weighted output cannot represent a zero-weight control with a nonzero
homogeneous numerator (a direction at infinity); request homogeneous output.
A zero numerator and zero weight is representable with zero Euclidean
coordinates. Nonzero weights that round to zero and overflowing returned
components are errors. Homogeneous output can overflow even when a weighted
representation fits; select the representation explicitly when needed.
No partial curve escapes on admission, arithmetic, work or cancellation errors.

Limits remain degree 0..16 and 65536 final controls. The call uses an
8,000,000-step work cap and the shared 65536-bit reduced-fraction cap.
Sorting is O(m log m), span lookup O(m log n), knot merging/output O(n+m),
and local coefficient work
O(m*degree*dimension), excluding bounded big-integer arithmetic; working exact
control storage is O(degree*dimension), with O(n+m) output storage.

and checks its output through the same native-backed BASIC APIs.
Evidence when accepted: `output/nurbs-refinement-2026-10-27/validation.json`.
