documents.html:
Changelog

Consolidated revision 1 — October 22, 2026

  • Consolidate the current tested master and installer display correction into one revision 1 baseline. Retire older release artifacts and source forks only after replacement validation and preservation of user programs/settings.
  • Keep runtime version 0.8.2; use Debian epoch 1 so the numbering reset remains newer than legacy revision 18 for package updates.

Unreleased — reliability and release gates

  • Extend CPU SPCG incomplete-Cholesky preconditioning from IC(0) to bounded symbolic fill levels IC(0) through IC(8). Keep JACOBI as the default and cap combined triangular-factor storage at one million entries.
  • Add optional CPU windowed-sinc alias suppression to RESAMPLE; keep linear interpolation as the default and enforce the shared math work limit.
  • Export a typed NativeSincResampler block API with constructor-reserved CPU buffers, rational phase, chunk-invariant state, atomic flush and bounded work.
  • Precompute bounded exact-phase CPU polyphase coefficients for common rational audio rates, retaining the checked fallback for larger phase sets.
  • Render live native synth and WAV output through bounded caller-owned stereo blocks, reusing mono and PCM scratch across writes.
  • Add CPU IDAHYBRID for residual DAE crossing events, direction filters, indexed reset callbacks and supported index-one consistency restoration. Bound reset callback work and event records; simultaneous resets compose in index order. Focused tests cover dense and preconditioned SPGMR trajectories, projection, atomic reset failures and close sequential root crossings.
  • Add the editable thermal_hysteresis_ida.bas CPU DAE workload; its six heater switches and algebraic heat-transfer states are checked against analytic heating/cooling intervals.
  • Add opt-in IDASOLVE(...,init$="AUTO") for CPU index-one initial-condition correction using the selected dense, SPGMR or KLU solver. Omitted or "SUPPLIED" initialization preserves the existing strict default.
  • Add CPU IMPLICITEVENTS for nonterminal vector events on adaptive backward- Euler trajectories, including optional analytic Jacobians and direction filters. Extend opt-in tangency detection to it; caller-supplied event-value tolerance localizes smooth same-sign minima on accepted steps. Limits and multiple-root constraints are documented and independently checked.
  • Add bounded eventscan subdivisions to terminal and nonterminal explicit and implicit event APIs. Terminal solvers stop at the first bracketed root; vector solvers localize multiple detected crossings on the original dense interpolant. Optional tangency minimization also runs per scan interval when tangenttol is set.
  • Add optional CPU eventdepth refinement to explicit and implicit terminal, vector and hybrid event APIs. Each level bisects configured scan intervals; combined work is capped at 4096 intervals per accepted step and default scan behavior remains unchanged.
  • Add CPU ODEHYBRID and IMPLICITHYBRID for bounded scalar-guard state resets. Event records preserve pre/post-reset states at a shared timestamp, and the explicit six-impact ball workload now uses native event restarts instead of a fabricated epsilon-time advance. Finite event scans and interpolation limits still apply.
  • Keep the windowed graphical installer within small displays using a bounded primary-display probe and per-process Qt scaling. Accept the real window frame bounds and avoid early-exit grep pipelines in installer launch checks. Revision 18 graphical BIOS installation passed; this layout correction is development source and still requires a rebuilt image.
  • Build a private revision 18 workstation candidate from one frozen source; retain package/image identity and disposable VM acceptance evidence. Correct ISO validation to extract the tracked ALSA restore rule before comparison; cover that path in the ISO fixture regression.
  • Add Ed25519-signed package-pair update metadata, safe administrator-owned public-key loading, expiry/revocation checks and retained authorization. A configured key store requires signatures for forward updates without blocking rollback/recovery. Add an offline publisher tool; no production key is generated or installed. Legacy checksum mode remains explicitly warned.
  • Harden root administration requests: atomically publish private window-ID markers and validate held nonblocking, non-following descriptors before root reads them. Reject wrong owners, unsafe modes, links, special files and replacements during validation. Retain the trusted-operator security model; this does not isolate hostile applications from the shared root X11 terminal.
  • Add separate per-session BASIC prompt recovery snapshots, AUTOSAVE controls and explicit RECOVER/EDIT discovery. Preserve unfinished drafts and originals; report checkpoint failures without blocking editing. Unhandled execution errors retain bounded statement, procedure and library context with hints for common mistakes, while preserving Error values and ON ERROR semantics.
  • Require the appliance target, audio supervisor and a responding private audio server before committing desktop updates. Clear audio service start limits when restarting after installation or rollback.
  • Add repeatable installed-system lifecycle acceptance on a new disposable disk: normal firmware boot, token-bound saved-state checks, supervised service recovery, offline package commit/rollback and guest-confirmed shutdown. Persistence verification now fails on missing files instead of recreating them.
  • Keep virtual PCI audio outputs awake between sounds to avoid suspend/reopen glitches, preserve exact failed-service names in diagnostic reports, repair Debian's duplicate ALSA restore-rule label without overriding local rules, and exercise actual program-window bounds in live close/audio acceptance.
  • Stream native music from queued note events instead of rendering complete tracks and a WAV before playback. Keep envelopes, oscillator phases, filters, waveguides and per-note settings across bounded audio blocks. Stream mixed native/SoundFont scores through the same output process, add a bounded device buffer, and retain WAV generation for explicit export. Check long-score startup, PCM equivalence, and paced playback continuity. Keep appliance/player gain at unity; save loudness corrections in BASIC scores. Use a configurable 250 ms device buffer for VM scheduling jitter, with regression checks for literal argument forwarding and session overrides.
  • Add broadcast batched TMM and differentiable TCONV1D/TCONV2D with explicit stride, symmetric padding and dilation. Bound forward/backward work, retain gradients on failed backward passes, and validate against independent NumPy contractions and finite differences. Connect numeric lists and DIM-array snapshots directly to WAVE; add image/geometry, music and learned-filter applications plus a concrete math completion roadmap.
  • Add SYMREFINE for conditional real simplification with exact sign deductions, square-root branches, inverse compositions and contradiction checks. Preserve original domains and explicit assumptions. Require suitable neighborhoods for calculus on guarded results, so a pointwise equality cannot create a false derivative. Add independent reference checks and a BASIC example.
  • Extend SYMANTIDERIV to polynomial-weighted exponential–trigonometric products and integer powers/products of affine sine and cosine functions. Use exact harmonic coefficients, checked conjugate pairing and polynomial coefficient recurrences; retain source domains and exceptional parameter conditions. Add generated independent reference checks, exact SymPy derivative identities, resource-limit regressions and a BASIC example.
  • Fix modern-mode SUM losing cancellation residuals or overflowing before a finite final answer. List, DIM-array, indexed, complex and broadcast reductions now accumulate exactly before final rounding. Integer-only results remain checked integers; legacy mode retains its previous behavior. Extend independent Fraction-reference checks and BASIC integration regressions.
  • Prepare revision 16 for the expanded math engine, including exact symbolic certificates, CPU tensor/autograd, sparse linear solvers and adaptive implicit integration. Allow the Debian build guest to recover from an official standard live seed when previous temporary BASIC build images are unavailable. Install BLAS/LAPACK and speech/media test dependencies inside the Debian builder. Source qualification does not imply image or physical-hardware acceptance.
  • Fill selected classic capability gaps with runtime EVAL, procedure libraries, indexed files, persistent debugger stops, same-session output windows, native menus, ON BREAK, TRANSLATE$, palette recoloring, PATTERN, LINPUT USING, sprite collision masks/borders and autonomous 2D animation. Retain bounded resources and document modern syntax and remaining parity limits. Validate with 94 explicit headless checks and seven isolated native X11 checks; diagnostics were not run. Evidence: output/classic-gap-implementation-2026-10-12/.
  • Add a manual-linked classic BASIC capability audit with 51 selected requirements, six independent BASIC examples and a reproducible runner for 60 focused checks. Correct stale parity claims; record missing/partial features and distinguish mock/headless evidence from hardware acceptance. That baseline audit changed no runtime behavior; its evidence remains separate from the subsequent gap-filling implementation.
  • Prevent HTTPS HTTP-client requests from following plaintext redirects; restore standard POST redirect methods and make transfer writes, reads and process completion interruptible with child cleanup and retained byte/time limits. Bound browser download filenames by UTF-8 bytes and report finalization errors per download instead of closing the browser. Add local HTTP/TLS, cancellation, size-limit and browser download regressions.
  • Harden the in-development firewall broker against IPv6 zone identifiers containing rule syntax and slow requests that delay rollback processing. Add isolated policy, transaction, persistence and protocol regressions; firewall UI, service packaging and live-system acceptance remain unfinished.
  • Invalidate release-test caches for embedded applications/helpers and require their runtime identity to match. Extract desktop launchers during ISO audits, repair the distro fixture, and exclude checkout Python bytecode from source identities while keeping installed-package inventories strict.
  • Make ordinary COMPILE interruptible with compiler-tree cleanup, bounded diagnostics and resource limits; supply the user bus in both appliance modes. Forward the desktop workspace to BASIC Console and reject linked console roots. Add explicit private-preview selection independently of release acceptance.
  • Add a desktop BASIC Console with the interactive programming prompt, shared editor workspace and Ctrl+Shift+C/V clipboard shortcuts. Add a visible Switch environment menu action and an explicit save-work confirmation for immediate switching; cancellation preserves the active session and startup preference.
  • Remove the browser engine's unsupported AutomationControlled feature override, which displayed a warning banner in the revision 15 desktop preview. Preserve the private control pipe and Chromium security defaults; previous streaming results using that workaround require renewed acceptance. Ignore shortcuts received before the embedded engine's READY handshake so pressing Ctrl+L during startup cannot turn into a startup error.
  • Prepare revision 15 private workstation packaging with an optional compiled desktop, persistent startup selection, complete embedded helper sources and desktop executable integrity checks. Default to direct BASIC and preserve user work. Exclude the development catalog from new images while retaining required embedded application sources. Add explicitly scoped private-image validation. Authenticate update health against the selected BASIC or packaged desktop executable and its matching window, retaining desktop identity for rollback.
  • Share embedded-source rebuild detection between normal launches and acceptance tools, including desktop applications and Python helpers. Preserve authorized Linux application access when executing installed programs or startup components. Correct the Rust 1.74 source gate to allow unsafe extern functions while still rejecting unsafe extern blocks.
  • Add a BASIC taskbar for the desktop's running app and program windows, including descendant windows, state indicators, hover labels, overflow pages and F6/arrow keyboard switching. Preserve the text-free resting desktop and existing dock. Ignore invisible dock controls in standalone apps; recover Files after a failed folder open without leaving the previous directory.
  • Confine default bundled app binary launches to ~/ModernBASIC instead of the process working directory. Create Programs without replacing user files and reject linked default workspace/Programs directories. Show BASIC-relative paths and a Browser downloads shortcut in Files, keeping browser internals out of its listing. Add a standalone Files launcher. Preserve explicit host workspace selection and ordinary compiled program defaults. Add regression coverage for blocked read/write/rename/delete, directory escape, inherited task roots and document preservation.
  • Launch Files, Text Editor, Writer, Sheet and Slides in independent BASIC windows through TASK APP. Preserve other apps when a parent window closes; allow parent task views to manage descendants. Add standalone editor/Office launchers. Replace Office bitmap text with system fonts, measured carets, cell alignment and slide wrapping. Handle window-manager close requests with discard confirmation.
  • Render vector application typography at the fitted window resolution, keeping text clear when a 1280-pixel interface runs on a smaller display, including buffered FLIP frames that also carry a logical-resolution bitmap. Add Noto Sans UI and Noto Sans Mono editor faces, larger controls, and fractional text metrics that keep carets and selections aligned during resizing. Preserve spaced font family names through scene serialization. Drain queued desktop typing before handling toolbar clicks so Save includes the final typed characters.
  • Add a BASIC-drawn browser application with embedded Chromium pages, live tabs, persistent profile/bookmarks/history, download controls and explicit confined uploads. Add WEB VIEW EMBED, bounded tab actions and TASK BROWSER for desktop launching. Retain the legacy temporary-profile WEB VIEW OPEN API.
  • Run BASIC programs from desktop Files or the editor with F5. Execute unsaved editor snapshots without overwriting files; keep each program in an independent window. Add a Programs view for switching, status, stopping and confirmed close, backed by bounded TASK commands in the linked runtime.
  • Use modern system sans-serif in desktop menus and controls, and system monospace in the editor. Add antialiased Pango/Cairo Unicode typography through FONT SYSTEM and matching TEXTWIDTH measurements for editor geometry. Keep portable built-in and bitmap fonts available to other BASIC programs.
  • Replace the desktop landing-page layout with a text-free wallpaper surface, application icons and a compact dock. Add an active application menu with hover highlighting, keyboard navigation, application launching and confirmed exit; explanatory copy no longer fills the desktop.
  • Make the desktop an explicit user choice: a bare interactive run.sh offers Desktop or No desktop, while --desktop and --no-desktop select directly. Direct BASIC and terminal commands remain available independently. Appliance packaging must preserve user choice; the current boot session is unchanged.
  • Add desktop editor mouse/keyboard selection, select all, cut/copy, selection replacement and selection-aware undo/redo. Compare undo results with saved text so undoing a saved edit still triggers unsaved-change confirmation. Preserve Unicode character offsets and document limits when replacing selected text. Expose modified navigation and Ctrl+A/C/X to graphical BASIC programs; SCREENCONTROL 5,text$ publishes UTF-8 text to the system clipboard.
  • Add a BASIC desktop application with file navigation, a text editor and a Chromium browser controller, plus native build/launch scripts and an isolated compiled-GUI acceptance check. The appliance boot session remains unchanged.
  • Add bounded DIR$, READFILE$, MKDIR and atomic WRITEFILE operations for BASIC applications. Extend compiled executables with explicit workspace, output and command-line options, standalone graphical lifecycle and headless self-tests; graphical sessions no longer expire at the instruction limit.
  • Preserve long clipboard pastes through the running-program keyboard queue and expose editor shortcuts and Tab to graphical BASIC applications.
  • Extend independent exact-executable regressions for portable BASIC core behavior, file fields, program replacement, and selection error recovery; distinguish language acceptance from the development-program catalog.
  • Refresh running MERGE programs immediately and relocate saved loop, return, error-resume, and debugger positions when statement indices change.
  • Clear non-COMMON declarations and stale error handlers when CHAIN starts another program, retaining declared types for COMMON values and arrays.
  • Route CASE expression failures through ON ERROR, including RESUME retry and RESUME NEXT recovery at the enclosing SELECT statement.
  • Use descriptor-relative Linux file deletion and renaming for BASIC and READY commands, preventing a swapped parent directory from escaping the file root.
  • Preserve the caller's declared type, fixed string width, and physical array destination through BYREF aliases, even when nested procedures shadow names.
  • Make INPUT# consume only its requested fields and continue across lines, preserving unread fields and the shared byte cursor for subsequent reads. Decode doubled quotes so WRITE#/INPUT# round-trip quoted Unicode and multiline strings while retaining input and storage limits.
  • Reuse cached X11 frames when windows are uncovered, skip content rebuilds on position-only moves, and bound mouse/window event batches so program output continues to be serviced while dragging. Add pixel-preservation and captured audio-continuity regressions.
  • Schedule VM previews at normal priority with a one-CPU aggregate ceiling and a 10 ms quota period, avoiding the long audio stalls allowed by the previous 75% quota over 100 ms.
  • Require installation ISOs to fit single-layer 4.7 GB DVDs; reject oversized or empty images before replacing any previously published output.
  • Build workstation-only images through the shared disk-backed Debian workflow, including native source tests, current editor/installer staging and exported artifact verification. Require the bootstrap/editor inputs before disk creation and budget 48 GiB for a fresh workstation build.
  • Separate current image instructions from historical notes and document the initial workstation release gates and experimental platform status.
  • Preserve representable complex multiplication, logarithms and negative integer powers at extreme magnitudes, including subnormal results.
  • Pass WEB GET/POST/DOWNLOAD URLs literally to curl, preventing brackets and braces from expanding one operation into multiple unintended requests.
  • Bound image/video probe output while reading, reject excess decoded image bytes before waiting, and terminate/reap decoder children on error. Input feeder threads are joined on cleanup and thread-start failure returns an error.
  • Share nesting and work limits across raw numerical evaluation and PIECEWISE; poll BREAK during nested evaluation instead of allowing unchecked recursive expression stacks and multiplicative numerical loops.
  • Save complete files by synced temporary-file replacement, preserving the previous destination on write failure and retaining its permissions.
  • Reserve image/media/SoundFont memory across capabilities and program windows, retain charges with asset ownership, and reuse equivalent local asset paths. Preflight SoundFont sample chunks and allocate their sample storage once; account separately for metadata and decode working space.
  • Bound text and binary program storage consistently; rejected loads, merges and numbered edits preserve existing source.
  • Replace broad catalog error suppression with declared per-program external dependencies; reject missing-line errors and abnormal process exits.
  • Retain unfinished structured programs during numbered entry, AUTO, EDIT, DELETE, RENUM and MERGE; failed execution checks preserve the draft and cannot run stale source. EDIT a source filename to reopen unfinished blocks for repair.
  • Add non-executing CHECK and read-only INSPECT at READY, including scoped variables, record fields and literal-index array elements during STOP/STEP. Program storage and session stability guarantees remain unchanged.
  • Provision missing examples atomically without replacing user files or following user links, including when the provision marker is absent or after an upgrade.
  • Run catalog probes in independent disposable source/fixture copies so BASIC file statements cannot modify the maintained examples or other test cases.
  • Embed an offline programming guide and ship four beginner lessons plus installed editor, language and audio references on every platform.
  • Use one verified master-source snapshot for all Debian deployment profiles, including runtime code, helpers, packaging, tests, assets and supplied notices. Centralize the candidate revision and target matrix in release.json (revision 14).
  • Reject mismatched complete release identities before image assembly and check the snapshot again before publishing package/image output. Preserve an existing package instead of silently replacing the same release filename.
  • Check build storage and host tools before launching a release VM; keep previous accepted images separate from new candidates.
  • Report the actual Cargo target directory from build.sh.
  • Resolve VM previews from the accepted current release and reject ambiguous images instead of falling back to a hard-coded older revision.
  • Tokenize compact direct commands like stored statements, resume the direct line after GOSUB/RETURN, and reject branches into procedure bodies without leaving stale return frames.
  • Make stored DATA available before the first RUN and refresh its cursor after a successful program replacement while preserving it after failed edits.
  • Preserve explicit array types across REDIM and validate local/STATIC whole arrays correctly when passed BYREF. Reject incompatible PRESERVE type changes and record/primitive replacements before committing any resize.
  • Apply default-type declarations atomically, report storage failures, and honor explicit suffixes when reading or swapping uninitialized scalar values.
  • Enforce file byte limits on binary-byte and random-record reads even if a file grows after OPEN; rejected reads preserve logical cursors and record buffers.
  • Keep multibyte LSET/RSET values within their byte-sized RANDOM file fields without splitting UTF-8 characters or overwriting adjacent fields.
  • Update spaced GO TO and GO SUB destinations during RENUM.
  • Honor DEFSTR in READ, INPUT, LINE INPUT, DIM, implicit arrays and REDIM, including scoped arrays and numeric suffix/declaration overrides.
  • Enforce per-file byte limits on graphics exports, including PNG conversion, screenshots and default graph outputs, before replacing existing files.
  • Keep FOR, WHILE, DO and REPEAT loop frames local to each structured procedure invocation, including recursive calls and empty FOR ranges.
  • Execute deeply nested inline IF chains without recursive host-stack growth, and bind inline ELSE branches to their matching IF in stored and direct code.
  • Make MID$ assignment read local, STATIC and BYREF string values, accept typed string names, and preserve commas inside nested argument expressions.
  • Accept default-type ranges with identical endpoints, such as DEFSTR A-A.
  • Preserve finite uniform-distribution results across opposite large bounds, annuity calculations near zero interest, relative IRR convergence, harmonic means of subnormal values, and negative gamma reflection near underflow.
  • Add focused runtime regressions and permanent BASIC artifact reproducers for these cases.
  • Add a BASIC-authored browser and optional Linux Chromium surface through WEB VIEW, with owned private profiles, navigation/events, explicit network grants, bounded pipe control and Widevine capability checks. Commercial DRM playback and deployment acceptance are distinct from engine capability.
  • Fix retained MP4 playback when container metadata follows the media data by providing a seekable, protocol-restricted decoder cache.
  • Keep sequential-file LOC/EOF accurate after invalid UTF-8 and oversized lines; consumed input remains consumed as specified by the language contract.
  • Enforce append size limits across concurrent channels and program sessions.
  • Track Unix advisory locks by open-file identity, including hard-link aliases, renames, unlinks, and reuse of an old filename.
  • Add removable-drive identity and volume controls with confirmed mount/unmount, whole-drive power-off/eject, busy-device reporting, stale-device checks and confined UDisks permissions. Removal never forces a busy filesystem.
  • Add graphical keyboard layout/variant selection with timed typing preview and automatic revert, saved graphical-map restoration at BASIC startup, and confirmed persistent time-zone selection through a dedicated confined helper account.
  • Add graphical Bluetooth discovery, pairing confirmation and masked PIN entry, connect/disconnect, explicit trust and removal. Run a fixed pairing helper under its own non-login account; restrict agent prompts to the selected device and cancel daemon operations when the user cancels.
  • Add graphical Wi-Fi discovery, NetworkManager password/hidden-network dialogs, saved-network controls and radio/disconnect actions. Keep credentials out of command lines, use temporary profiles until connection succeeds, and restore the previous adapter connection after failure or cancellation.
  • Stage a separate offline ModernBASIC update/recovery service with retained previous packages, checksum/source/architecture checks, dependency preflight, durable transaction state, desktop health checks, rollback and boot recovery. Show its public status alongside Debian update scheduling in SETTINGS.
  • Add an unprivileged OS settings center (SETTINGS) with real audio output names, default output, connector, volume, mute, and a bounded left/right test. Include hardware/update status and existing administration instructions.
  • Add the appliance first-run checklist and explicit completion (SETUP to revisit). Preserve native display rollback through DISPLAY and from settings. Settings dialogs and audio-test processes close with their BASIC session.
  • Keep the system hub available after invalid EDIT arguments.
  • Route READY LOAD/MERGE/SAVE/LOADB/SAVEB/VERIFY/COPY through bounded, nonblocking sandbox file access. COPY to the same file or a hard-link alias preserves contents; binary program reads and writes share the 64 MiB limit.
  • Parse NAME/COPY separators outside quoted filenames and reject renaming the current workspace or its ancestors.
  • Reject trailing arguments to TRON, TROFF, WEND, and RESUME NEXT; validate RESUME syntax before changing the active error context.
  • Keep diagnostic collection working with unavailable/corrupt build metadata, reject non-object saved reports cleanly, and bound subprocess output/time.
  • Classify reports as Linux kernel, Modern BASIC environment, OS integration, or unsure. Service failures default to integration, without guessing root cause.
  • Add the central release/report portal with private developer queues, category and status history, consent-based submission, and validated resumable platform downloads. Include deployment configs and HTTP security/workflow tests. No replacement ISO images are published by this change.
  • Extend source validation to Python services and extensionless OS helpers; allow staged appliance contract checks to select an exact executable.
  • Added 32 case-insensitive names for default screen/text colors in hub commands, startup options, and saved preferences. COLORS lists the names; hexadecimal colors remain supported. Invalid color input leaves the hub available for another command.
  • Bound both matrix constructor dimensions before allocation, including zero rows or columns, so oversized empty matrices report BASIC errors.
  • Reject special files without blocking sandboxed Linux opens; validate the descriptor before truncation. Added FIFO timeout coverage for all file modes, LOAD, and SAVE.
  • Use row-relative pivot selection for DET, INVERSE, and LINSOLVE, preserving small nonsingular matrices and matrices with differently scaled rows.
  • Preserve small components in complex square roots and avoid intermediate overflow/underflow in complex division by separating binary exponents.
  • Normalize IRR cash flows before convergence checks so changing their common scale does not change the result.
  • Added numerical and empty-matrix artifact regressions. These fixes preserve the revision 1 Values, Resources, and Files contract rows; no language syntax or contract revision changes.
  • Fixed atomic INPUT/INPUT# storage preflight when replacements reuse existing payload and when BYREF destinations alias the same variable.
  • Preserved whole-array element identity when forwarding a BYREF element into a nested procedure.
  • Added generated loop/procedure and input-transaction checks, a permanent executable regression corpus, and a checked core language stability contract.
  • Added measurable session lifecycle soaks, paced PCM fidelity/gap probes, repeatable X11 renderer cycling, and exact executable/Debian-artifact checks that record hashes and never silently rebuild the selected artifact.
  • Added per-change MSRV/stable CI and scheduled long-session validation. Hardware certification and the reported full-workload live-audio issue remain explicit outstanding release requirements.

0.8.2 Neon Depth Runner acceptance - 2026-09-02

  • Added Neon Depth Runner, a self-contained playable game demonstrating selectable HD-through-UHD screens, generated/resident mapped textures, shared sprite instances, XYZ control and motion, camera/light changes, retained objects/pixels, projected collision, pause/restart behavior, and a deterministic rendered self-test.
  • Extended appliance QEMU validation to load the bundled game, generate its assets as the unprivileged runtime user, start gameplay through virtual hardware input, and require a changed live game frame before accepting the ISO.
  • Made sprite motion/depth/collision and perspective-object query functions evaluate string-variable IDs consistently with their matching statements. The loop-driven game and a focused regression cover this pooled-entity path.

0.8.2 modern game screens and resident 3D sprite world - 2026-09-01

  • Added named logical game resolutions for 720p, 900p, Full HD, QHD, 3440x1440 ultrawide, and 4K while retaining independent fit/stretch host scaling.
  • Extended SPRITE IMAGE with an (x,y,z) form. Mapped sprites now occupy the retained perspective world, share load-time-decoded texture pixels, project and depth-sort with all other entities, receive ambient/point-light tint, move on three axes, and participate in projected collision checks.
  • Added a bounded 64 MiB per-render-thread cache for immutable engine-private textures. Cache hits reuse the same pixel allocation; transparency-key variants remain isolated and source files are never reopened per frame.
  • Added table-level resolution coverage, model-level world-command checks, allocation-identity cache tests, and black-box BASIC tests that delete the source texture before rendering the live XYZ world.

0.8.2 native sprite and font asset workflow - 2026-09-01

  • Added image-backed named sprites with scaling, exact-color transparency, movement, deterministic motion, collision queries/traps, and normal buffered rendering through SPRITE IMAGE.
  • Added portable bitmap-font sheets selectable through FONT, including cached decoding, tinted alpha/brightness masks, and FONT BUILTIN restore.
  • Added C128-inspired graphical EDIT SPRITE and EDIT FONT hub tools. They export eight 24x21 sprite assets and a complete 96-glyph 8x8 ASCII sheet in directly consumable PPM form.
  • Added black-box rendering/collision/key-transparency coverage, hub routing, bounded headless editor-loop probes, and QEMU checks that require both editor windows to render distinct content and remain stable. Updated the embedded language manual and classic-capability matrix.

0.8.2 independent production hardening - 2026-09-01

  • Added a separate seven-test hardening target using model-based arithmetic, binary-image mutation, parallel-session stress, live symlink swapping, hostile CLI input, and sandboxed printer-output probes. The target passes normally and under AddressSanitizer.
  • Routed default LPRINT/LPRINT USING output to a bounded spool beneath the configured output sandbox. Removed automatic physical-printer discovery and the predictable shared /tmp spool; explicit host spool overrides reject symlinks, use close-on-exec descriptors and private creation permissions, and obey the configured per-file byte limit.
  • Replaced the graphical shell's predictable shared /tmp error log with stderr diagnostics, corrected the manual-matrix source path and native 64-bit line-number contract, fixed a README code fence, and reconciled the verified catalog at 360 numbered programs after removing a zero-byte scratch artifact.

0.8.2 Music Forge responsiveness update - 2026-08-28

  • Made SOUND OFF discard native and sampled score queues as well as stopping live playback. Interactive music programs can now stop, rebuild, and restart a score without stale notes accumulating in memory.
  • Changed Music Forge playback to background operation so its graphics and keyboard loop remain responsive while a score plays. S stops playback and P restarts it from a clean queue.
  • Removed the mouse-release busy loop and compressed consecutive empty score slots into longer rests before MML conversion, reducing input stalls and playback preparation work.

0.8.2 modern-native graphics fast path r2 - 2026-08-28

  • Applied the exact rustfmt layout required by cargo fmt --check so the complete verify.sh gate can proceed to compilation and tests.

0.8.2 modern-native graphics fast path - 2026-08-28

  • Kept graphics GET arrays fully compatible with ordinary BASIC array reads and writes while caching their dense ARGB pixels behind the array. Repeated PUT calls now share that cache instead of rebuilding a framebuffer-sized vector from sparse array values every frame; any BASIC element write invalidates and safely rebuilds the cache.
  • Added a full-frame opaque PUT PSET path with scanline framebuffer copies. It avoids destination reads, per-pixel raster-action dispatch, repeated dirty rectangle expansion, and a second framebuffer-sized result allocation.
  • Added automatically selected raster_rle retention for compressible copied frames, while preserving the established inline raster representation for images where run-length encoding would be larger.
  • Added a native-size device-bitmap renderer path. Exact PUT rasters are no longer bilinearly resampled with floating-point calculations at every pixel, and retained bitmap payloads use shared storage when scene state is cloned.
  • Changed the automatic-PSET presentation regression to verify the rendered white pixel instead of requiring one obsolete Artist command spelling. Added cache reuse/invalidation, compact-raster validation, scanline blit, opacity, and framebuffer correctness coverage.
  • Added GRAPHICS_PERFORMANCE.md with the recommended draw-once, GET, PUT, dynamic-overlay, and single-FLIP animation pattern.

0.8.2 modern-native true-color graphics refresh - 2026-08-28

  • Added native RGB(red,green,blue) and RGBA(red,green,blue,alpha) constructors. Calls now produce canonical true-color strings instead of falling through to BASIC array lookup and reporting ?bad subscript.
  • Added scanline raster batching for consecutive identity-coordinate PSET operations. Pixel paintings retain one command per contiguous row run while classic numeric palette colors and general transformed drawing retain their established behavior.
  • Added expression, color-range, renderer-order, framebuffer, and runnable true-color gradient regressions.

0.8.2 modern-native refresh - 2026-08-27

  • Corrected the complete catalog gate: explicit negative programs now have exact required diagnostics, disabled WAV exporters are classified as environmental probes, and an expected error that disappears or changes is a verification failure. Repaired three flipbook declarations, two Koto programs, one malformed SOUND statement, one obsolete note-analysis test, and normal PLAY score$,beats LOAD-manifest handling.
  • Added one stable install.sh entry point. A normal installation is now ./install.sh; release validation is ./install.sh --verify; startup remains ./run.sh.
  • Made the asynchronous BREAK regression deterministic: the test now steps through its RAM setup before starting the interrupt timer, then verifies BREAK during WAIT and confirms the active program and variable survive. This removes a scheduler race exposed when LOAD-time preparation takes more than the test's former 20 ms head start.
  • Moved statement splitting, line indexing, structured-control validation, and DATA collection to the successful LOAD/edit boundary. Interactive RUN now clones one resident execution-plan handle and resets only BASIC runtime state; it neither reparses the stored program nor reopens prepared assets. Added a regression that deletes a bitmap after LOAD and proves RUN still succeeds from the decoded in-memory object.
  • Made READY. a strict successful-preparation boundary. Failed LOAD and LOADB requests now report LOAD FAILED; OLD PROGRAM RETAINED. without printing a misleading READY line for the rejected program.
  • Kept live execution separate from optional output creation: ordinary PLAY, graphics drawing, DISPLAY, SOUND RESUME, END, and STOP write no files. Export statements remain explicit opt-in operations.
  • Replaced the live VIDEO soundtrack's /proc/self/fd FFmpeg input with the native inherited pipe:N protocol. This fixes the target-machine encoder exit status 250 (ENXIO) and removes a needless Linux procfs dependency. Encoder failures now retain a bounded FFmpeg diagnostic instead of hiding stderr.
  • Corrected the release formatting detected by cargo fmt --check and removed the unused legacy articulation helper and its isolated test. Sampled note gates continue to come from the active per-voice SoundFontDsp settings.
  • Restored the declared Rust 1.74 minimum-toolchain compatibility by using edition-2021 FFI block syntax and explicit std::mem::size_of paths. This also fixes native builds with Ubuntu 24.04's Rust 1.75 packages.
  • Consolidated sampled playback and WAV export onto one SoundFont score renderer and one fixed-gain PCM encoder. Removed the unused sequential note-on/render path, raw voice-zero exception, per-chunk peak normalization, and gain pumping; quiet passages now retain their programmed level.
  • Removed unused additive/modal prototype modules and the no-op banjo body. Corrected banjo construction so it starts silent, selects only a physically playable string, gives the requested string stable full level, and excites only quiet harmonically related open strings.
  • Added four-program sound/graphics concurrency verification. The system hub remains separate from every program's READY. statement environment, and each program task retains independent graphics, input, interrupt, and audio ownership while host playback mixes simultaneous songs.
  • Made oscillator-limit integration tests select deterministic STANDARD explicitly instead of depending on the host-selected AUTO profile.
  • Extended verify.sh through release smoke tests and a complete 346-program catalog pass with canonical loading plus bounded, classified headless runs.
  • Kept ModernBASIC as one native Rust language and documented the boundary between compatible BASIC semantics and virtualized or native host services.
  • Made aspect-preserving graphics fitting the actual shell default; deliberate non-uniform stretching remains available through --graphics-scale stretch.
  • Made the hardware-scanned AUTO synthesis arrangement the modern default, while retaining explicit deterministic profiles and exact voice/oscillator overrides.
  • Raised the guarded non-interactive execution budget from 100,000 to 10,000,000 statements. Interactive READY. sessions remain unlimited until completion or BREAK.
  • Added build-native.sh for host-CPU optimized builds and source-check.sh for compiler-independent structural validation.
  • Integrated the current 346-program catalog, repaired duplicate/out-of-order lines in two Persian music programs, and added a native 64-bit/core-BASIC conformance program.
  • Kept optional third-party SoundFont banks outside the source archive and documented the exact bank names required by sampled-instrument programs.

0.8.2 — 2026-08-19

  • Added validated LOCATE, CSRLIN, VIEW PRINT, HOME, HTAB, VTAB, TEXTCOLOR, key-abortable fractional-second SLEEP, and live bare INKEY$. The new identifier-encoded statement names remain assignable when followed by =. Text cursor state, region changes, output, and color events stay causally ordered for the X11 shell.
  • Corrected Unicode PRINT/WIDTH column tracking and wrapping, Microsoft comparison-before-NOT precedence, and numeric PRINT USING type checks. Invalid text coordinates now raise IllegalQuantity, and HOME uses the active print-region origin.
  • Added generation-tracked lazy synchronization from retained Artist scenes to each graphics framebuffer, providing coherent pixels for future query and capture statements. Fullscreen startup now requests managed EWMH _NET_WM_STATE_FULLSCREEN instead of using override_redirect.
  • Isolated PCM playback and speech queues per interpreter/program window and recognized both MODERNBASIC_NO_AUDIO and MODERN64BASIC_NO_AUDIO consistently across synthesis, speech, and shell status reporting.
  • Added retained FLIPBOOK CREATE/REMOVE/CLEAR, paced PLAY FLIPBOOK, and direct VIDEO EXPORT so hundreds of complete still images form one bounded movie asset without a duplicate video engine. Extended PLAY explicitly to sandboxed local AUDIO and VIDEO while preserving classic note notation. Added a 72-frame old-paper stickman demo and a 120-frame 960x540 one-leaf photo-detail demo with an anchored bending/turning texture mesh, and produced verified GIF/H.264 artifacts from both.
  • Added BRUSH with size, hardness, opacity, and flow; PNG/JPEG/WebP/BMP/TIFF BITMAP import through fixed FFmpeg arguments; alpha-preserving premultiplied bilinear bitmap scaling; the organized BITMAP WARP subcommand for anchored bend, turn, angle, and light; flipbook letterboxing; and raster-first PNG output that preserves imported photographic pixels and compositing. Dynamic string graphics identifiers now evaluate correctly instead of being mistaken for literal names.
  • Added explicit MIXER voice,synth-level,midi-level routing so each PLAY voice can use the computer generator, the MIDI/SoundFont instrument, or both sample-accurately layered. Native and sampled queues are now combined for live output and WAVEFILE instead of one queue replacing the other.
  • Retained validated SING scores for optional WAVEFILE export. Vocals now render at 44.1 kHz, append in source order on their own timeline, and mix sample-accurately with native and SoundFont music.
  • Completed the native instrument-building core with a configurable bounded bank of 1 through 8 per-voice OSCILLATOR slots, SYNTHPROFILE host scanning, per-program VOICES/OSCILLATORS overrides, and per-voice multimode FILTER, FILTERADSR, plus simultaneous target-specific LFO controls, GLIDE, and DRIVE. These are independent BASIC controls; no catch-all SYNTH statement was introduced. Added compact patch and arrangement examples plus magnetic_dawn.bas, an original eight-voice extended native-synthesis showcase.
  • Established one ModernBASIC tone interface, SOUND frequency,voice,duration with optional per-note level and sweep controls. WAVE, ADSR, PULSEWIDTH, VOL, STEREO, and FILTER remain independent voice controls, and SOUND can queue complete oscillator tone sequences without PLAY note notation. Removed the reversed voice-first signature and its unrelated delay argument rather than retaining a compatibility overload.
  • Made interactive LOAD parse and retain distinct static SoundFont assets before committing the program or returning the prompt; failed preparation is atomic. RUN reuses those banks, and live sampled playback now writes bounded 2,048-frame chunks instead of rendering the entire song before its first sound, with ADSR and per-voice DSP state continuous across chunks.
  • Corrected the raster font's column-major glyph interpretation so printable ASCII renders as upright English instead of rotated symbol-like shapes. Large capitals, digits, and presentation punctuation now use a dependency-free antialiased geometric display face instead of enlarged 5x7 cells. Added a 15-second Full-HD capabilities presentation with dancing type, real sprite motion/collision state, gradients, compositing, curves, generated stereo music, and data-driven graphics.
  • Defined SCREEN as a resolution-independent logical graphics device in the native shell. Window resizing now preserves and centers its aspect ratio by default, pointer coordinates map only through the fitted viewport, and black bars are outside MOUSEINSIDE(). Added compact, desktop, HD, and Full HD host window profiles, an explicit stretch mode, physical-display clamping, atomic failed screen changes, and repeated buffer/resize/extreme-geometry stress coverage.
  • Tightened CLS invariants: it resets the selected graphics buffer, sprites, pixels, and drawing point without touching the visible front buffer before FLIP; argument-free split-screen clears now clear both text and graphics. Regressions prove retained rendering cannot preserve shapes removed by a clear. The capabilities presentation now defaults to file-free live BASIC, follows wall-clock time, and resets animation and native synthesized music together; recording is an explicit source switch.
  • Added bounded program-driven VIDEO START/FRAME/STOP export to MP4, WebM, and GIF through a fixed FFmpeg encoder interface, plus a 360-frame 1920x1080, 60 fps graphics-only cinematic animation demo and real H.264 acceptance coverage. VIDEO START now accepts an optional sandboxed WAV soundtrack for MP4/WebM. MP4 uses a high-detail CRF 17 real-time H.264 encode with eight bounded encoder threads. Batch runs can explicitly raise the otherwise unchanged safety guard with --max-steps for bounded long-form rendering. Generated graphics, audio, and video can use an independent --output-root; packaged runs gather them in the root-level output/ folder instead of the BASIC source catalog. Soundtrack muxing pads short audio and clips long audio at video EOF, avoiding an equal-duration codec-timebase race that could close the final frame pipe.
  • Activated true linear/radial gradient paints and all advertised blend modes in raster/video output, corrected radial-gradient radii, added subpixel edge coverage for thin/thick lines and polygon slopes, added simultaneous fill/stroke rendering for core primitives, and made rounded rectangles genuinely rounded. LINE ...,color,width now honors expression and variable widths instead of confusing them with the legacy B/BF box mode. Headless animation no longer rerenders the accumulated scene after every drawing statement; the HD demo's measured single-frame time fell from 13.86 seconds to 0.15 seconds. Full-HD raster storage is now binary32, exact common scene prefixes are retained in a 32 MiB cache, and final RGB packing is parallel. The capabilities benchmark improved from 12.1 to 36.1 generated fps without changing its 8-bit output bytes; sustained 1080p H.264 generation reaches 34.8 fps.
  • Added deterministic sprite velocity/acceleration stepping with live position/motion queries, logical-screen mouse polling, and a real bounded nonblocking INKEY$() queue for interactive graphical programs.
  • Defined the Amiga 500 creative-programming profile and its modern hardware, safety, dialect, and no-photo/no-video-editor boundaries.
  • Added per-voice DSP voice,drive,tone,presence,compression,gate for sampled amplifier saturation, cabinet tone, pick/strike presence, dynamics, and note-release articulation before voices are mixed. Steel Thunder now gives all ten instrument voices role-specific DSP configurations.
  • Added --soundfont-root so multi-user installations can keep one shared, administrator-owned instrument backend while each account uses a separate writable --file-root. Added common system-wide backend discovery paths.
  • Replaced Steel Thunder's synthesized-sounding lead with paired clean/distorted CC0 Fender samples and replaced its doubled pitch-shifted/GM bass with a dedicated CC0 Yamaha RBX picked-bass bank. The compact clean lead avoids a 425 MiB decoded bank in every concurrent process. Explicit low-sustain ADSR shaping emphasizes the recorded pick transient on both guitar and bass.
  • Added per-voice and inclusive voice-range SOUNDFONT bindings so one BASIC PLAY score can combine multiple sampled banks on a shared timeline. Fixed one-based BASIC voice instrument selection, made END/STOP wait for queued live playback, and kept file creation exclusive to explicit WAVEFILE use.
  • Kept optional banks as backend hardware in the dedicated root-level soundfont/ directory and made that read-only asset root independent of READY's current directory, fixing OS error 2 after CD or nested loads.
  • Applied explicit per-voice BASIC ADSR settings to sampled SoundFont output; voices without ADSR retain the instrument bank's natural envelope.
  • Added sandboxed SOUNDFONT path$ selection for real sampled instruments, automatic MuseScore General/FluidR3 system-bank discovery, and an installer for the free MIT-licensed MuseScore General SF2 and its license. Added BASIC control of sampled volume, pan, note velocity, expression, modulation, sustain, pitch bend, reverb, and chorus.
  • Renamed the product to ModernBASIC; the Cargo package, library crate, and executable are now modernbasic, and configuration variables use the MODERNBASIC_ prefix.
  • Printed the classic READY. line whenever RUN or CONT returns control, including completion, STOP/BREAK, and runtime errors, while correctly ending any unterminated PRINT line first. The status bar now labels Ctrl+U as the uppercase/mixed-case input toggle.
  • Added graphical list editing: Ctrl+Up/Ctrl+Down automatically capture and navigate a loaded program, F2 remains an explicit LIST/edit entry, the normal cursor keys edit selected lines, and Enter replaces them without retyping. Ordinary Up/Down retain command and numbered-statement history behavior.
  • Prevented X11 special keysyms such as Ctrl+Left from being truncated into control letters, bounded cached line indices, invalidated stale line caches on command transitions, and kept F-key commands out of a running program's INPUT stream.
  • Replaced prompt-text guessing with an explicit READY event from the REPL, so program output cannot accidentally enable command-only keyboard actions.
  • Made existing sandboxed file and directory lookup case-insensitive, allowing uppercase BASIC input such as CD EXAMPLES to reach packaged lowercase host paths without weakening canonical root and symlink-escape checks.
  • Completed the READY file browser with BASIC-relative path reporting, subfolder/file/byte totals, directories-first sorting, root and parent navigation, both slash styles, compact CD.., wildcard listings, and bounded recursive TREE browsing that never follows links.
  • Made programs the complete visible root name and suppressed the canonical /home/... prefix from PWD, DIR, TREE, and STATUS. Displayed paths such as programs/music can be passed back to every READY file command.
  • Made Ctrl+Escape the sole hard BREAK shortcut and return graphics/demo views to text so the result is visible; plain Escape remains a local view/cancel key without interrupting BASIC.
  • Added a non-audio BASIC conformance example and included it plus sandboxed WRITE#/INPUT# round-trip behavior in the release smoke test.
  • Ported the attached 210-file runnable program catalog to the current 0.8 statement set instead of adding removed legacy commands to the interpreter. Corrected duplicate/out-of-order numbered lines, replaced the TCP chat and character-ROM editor demos with portable programs, and rewrote old audio programs around WAVE, ADSR, VOL, PLAY, SOUND, and WAIT.
  • Unified native oscillator playback with the SoundFont Linux backend: paplay is preferred and aplay is the fallback for both paths. Added audio-test.sh, deterministic RIFF/WAVE smoke coverage, and catalog source checks that reject legacy statements and duplicate or unsorted line numbers.
  • Made the packaged programs directory the default BASIC user root, with --file-root retained as an explicit override.
  • Made shell program.bas actually load the requested program.
  • Implemented native interruptible WAIT milliseconds and classic WAIT port,mask[,xor] over the bounded virtual port device.
  • Corrected WHILE/WEND pre-test skipping, nesting, frame reuse, and unmatched-loop diagnostics.
  • Added colon-aware inline ELSE and validated nested block IF...THEN...ELSE...END IF forms.
  • Added DO/LOOP top/bottom conditions, BBC REPEAT/UNTIL, and structured EXIT DO/FOR/WHILE/REPEAT.
  • Added nested standard SELECT CASE with values, inclusive ranges, relational clauses, strings, and defaults, plus BBC CASE...OF/WHEN/OTHERWISE.
  • Added XOR/BBC EOR, integer DIV and \, Microsoft-style rounded integer operands, bare RND, BIN$, and the checked FACTORIAL alias.
  • Added spaced GO SUB, one-or-more-parameter numeric DEF FN, ASCII UCASE$/LCASE$, and C128 hexadecimal-string DEC fallback.
  • Added LINE INPUT # with bounded whole-line reads that preserve commas and empty lines.
  • Added MS/GW-BASIC OPEN mode$,#channel,path$ shorthand while retaining the standard OPEN path$ FOR mode AS #channel grammar and file sandbox.
  • Added bounded, atomic Dartmouth CHANGE conversion between strings and numeric character-code arrays.
  • Added bounded, atomic REDIM and REDIM PRESERVE for numeric and string arrays. Preservation keeps the complete overlapping region of same-rank multidimensional shapes. Corrected ERASE to release sparse value storage and full reserved array capacity.
  • Added immutable numeric and string CONST declarations with calculated and comma-separated initializers, typed assignment, CLEAR persistence, and protection across scalar assignment, input, data, swap, and string-lvalue paths.
  • Added validated multi-line SUB/END SUB procedures with value parameters, recursive and nested CALL, per-call local scalars, scalar SHARED and persistent STATIC storage, EXIT SUB, classic GOSUB interoperability, shared stack/storage limits, atomic argument binding, and branch-boundary enforcement.
  • Added validated multi-line numeric and string FUNCTION/END FUNCTION declarations with typed return-slot assignment, EXIT FUNCTION, recursion, local/SHARED/STATIC scope, calls to SUB, expression and READY. use, bounded depth/storage, and lazy IF, loop, SELECT CASE, and PIECEWISE evaluation. Corrected WHILE conditions to run exactly once per iteration.
  • Added coherent procedure argument modes: parameters remain BYVAL by default, may state BYVAL explicitly, and may use exact-type BYREF aliases to scalars, array elements, record fields, and record-array field elements. Aliases forward through nested/recursive SUB and FUNCTION calls, mutate immediately, and do not duplicate retained-storage charges.
  • Added explicit exact-type whole-array BYREF name() formals and name() actuals, including nested forwarding, record-field arrays, READ, MAT, REDIM [PRESERVE], ERASE, fixed strings, and scope isolation. Exact-type whole-record arrays use BYREF name() AS type, alias every field without a copy, forward through nested SUB/FUNCTION calls, resize atomically, and propagate erasure back to the caller.
  • Added per-call local primitive arrays declared with procedure DIM, plus persistent STATIC name(bounds) arrays for SUB and FUNCTION. Recursive frames isolate physical storage, return releases local capacity, CLEAR and CHAIN release STATIC capacity, and primitive AS metadata is restored transactionally so identically named procedures cannot contaminate types.
  • Added fully scoped procedure-local and persistent STATIC record arrays. Recursive calls isolate every physical field array, local capacity is released on return, STATIC fields survive calls and reset on CLEAR, and record/type metadata rolls back atomically on failed dimensioning.
  • Added scoped typed primitive and record scalars inside SUB/FUNCTION, plus STATIC name AS type. Record fields inherit the base record's SHARED or STATIC scope; recursive locals isolate values and metadata, STATIC types cannot silently change, and CLEAR/CHAIN release both values and type state.
  • Added exact-type whole-record assignment for scalar records and indexed record-array elements, including values reached through whole-record BYREF formals. Every source field is captured before writing and late storage-limit failures roll back all destination fields.
  • Added nested user-defined record fields with forward TYPE references, pre-execution undefined-type and cycle rejection, multi-level scalar/array access, exact-type whole-subrecord assignment, and root/subrecord typed-array aliases that forward through nested procedures. Local, STATIC, REDIM, ERASE, fixed-string, and retained-storage behavior reuse the same atomic record machinery.
  • Corrected CALL argument tokenization so procedure names beginning with a reserved prefix, such as SCALEALL, FORWARD, or MODIFY, remain identifiers while classic compact control syntax stays unchanged.
  • Added LBOUND/UBOUND over real stored shapes, with multidimensional, OPTION BASE, record-field, local, STATIC, REDIM, and whole-array alias coverage.
  • Made SPRITE/MOVESPRITE visible in the built-in raster/SVG renderer, tracked per-buffer sprite geometry, and added live pair/any PCOLLISION queries. Added bounded, non-reentrant ON TIMER(...) GOSUB and `ON COLLISION GOSUB event traps with ON/OFF/STOP` lifecycle controls.
  • Added validated TYPE/END TYPE records and DIM ... AS type for scalar and array instances. Primitive numeric, dynamic string, and fixed-width string fields support dotted reads/writes, DATA/READ, console/file input, bounded atomic REDIM [PRESERVE], and record-aware ERASE.
  • Corrected token-stream serialization for every extension keyword beyond the historical one-byte range using an escaped 16-bit form; legacy token bytes remain unchanged. Qualified record identifiers now round-trip through source and binary forms, including the classic array(index).field spelling.
  • Corrected CLEAR/RUN state reset to discard active structured frames, persistent procedure STATIC values, and FUNCTION result handoff state together, preventing stale values and retained-storage accounting.
  • Corrected WRITE# to emit quoted, comma-delimited BASIC fields instead of PRINT# zone spacing, including embedded quotes and nested expressions.
  • Corrected ON ERROR/RESUME: plain RESUME retries the failing statement, RESUME NEXT advances once, loop depth is restored, the handler remains armed for later errors, and ON ERROR GOTO 0 disables trapping cleanly.
  • Completed inverse keyword mappings for NAME, LINE INPUT, and the internal default-type token.
  • Added editor, directory-root, statement-token, and native hardware regression coverage plus a statement-conformance reference.

0.8.1 — 2026-08-19

  • Preserved the attached 0.8.0 source as the authoritative branch instead of overwriting it with the differently structured 0.7 package.
  • Corrected SoundFont PLAY voice scheduling. Voice numbers are now converted to zero-based cursor indices correctly, and Vn changes both the cursor and MIDI channel for subsequent notes.
  • Added regression coverage for independent SoundFont voice cursors and MIDI channels.
  • Preserved left/right SoundFont samples so STEREO and PAN affect both live playback and WAV output instead of collapsing the result to mono.
  • Peak-normalized live SoundFont output is encoded and written in bounded blocks instead of allocating a second song-sized PCM buffer.
  • Live playback now prefers paplay and falls back to aplay.
  • Added dotted note-length coverage such as C4/8..
  • Removed unused mastering constants and corrected lint-sensitive code in the attached uncommitted audio changes.
  • Synchronized Cargo manifest and lockfile versions at 0.8.1.
  • Added release documentation, examples, verification scripts, an attachment comparison report, and the required RustySynth/MeltySynth MIT notice.
  • Removed repository history and Python bytecode from the distributable tree.

0.8.0 attachment baseline

  • Native ModernBASIC interpreter with 16-voice audio, SoundFont synthesis, speech, graphics, graphing, matrices, and a Linux/X11 shell.
  • Consolidated the earlier DSP/transcription experiment out of the runtime.
  • Removed the older separate MUSIC and SOUNDFONT statement families.
  • Corrected SoundFont generator parsing for banks without unused terminal padding.
  • Sampled scores retain per-PLAY mixer, controller, pitch, ADSR and DSP settings.
  • Added exact SoundFont preset names and optional INSTRUMENT bank selection; unavailable presets now report errors.
  • Improved Linux player startup fallback and retained bounded diagnostics; appliance playback now uses unity gain.
  • Restored sampled instruments in ten music programs that contained removed-command placeholders.

# Changelog

## Consolidated revision 1 — October 22, 2026

- Consolidate the current tested master and installer display correction into
  one revision 1 baseline. Retire older release artifacts and source forks only
  after replacement validation and preservation of user programs/settings.
- Keep runtime version 0.8.2; use Debian epoch 1 so the numbering reset remains
  newer than legacy revision 18 for package updates.

## Unreleased — reliability and release gates

- Extend CPU SPCG incomplete-Cholesky preconditioning from IC(0) to bounded
  symbolic fill levels IC(0) through IC(8). Keep JACOBI as the default and cap
  combined triangular-factor storage at one million entries.
- Add optional CPU windowed-sinc alias suppression to `RESAMPLE`; keep linear
  interpolation as the default and enforce the shared math work limit.
- Export a typed `NativeSincResampler` block API with constructor-reserved CPU
  buffers, rational phase, chunk-invariant state, atomic flush and bounded work.
- Precompute bounded exact-phase CPU polyphase coefficients for common
  rational audio rates, retaining the checked fallback for larger phase sets.
- Render live native synth and WAV output through bounded caller-owned stereo
  blocks, reusing mono and PCM scratch across writes.
- Add CPU `IDAHYBRID` for residual DAE crossing events, direction filters,
  indexed reset callbacks and supported index-one consistency restoration.
  Bound reset callback work and event records; simultaneous resets compose in
  index order. Focused tests cover dense and preconditioned SPGMR trajectories,
  projection, atomic reset failures and close sequential root crossings.
- Add the editable `thermal_hysteresis_ida.bas` CPU DAE workload; its six heater
  switches and algebraic heat-transfer states are checked against analytic
  heating/cooling intervals.
- Add opt-in `IDASOLVE(...,init$="AUTO")` for CPU index-one initial-condition
  correction using the selected dense, SPGMR or KLU solver. Omitted or
  `"SUPPLIED"` initialization preserves the existing strict default.
- Add CPU `IMPLICITEVENTS` for nonterminal vector events on adaptive backward-
  Euler trajectories, including optional analytic Jacobians and direction
  filters. Extend opt-in tangency detection to it; caller-supplied event-value
  tolerance localizes smooth same-sign minima on accepted steps. Limits and
  multiple-root constraints are documented and independently checked.
- Add bounded `eventscan` subdivisions to terminal and nonterminal explicit and
  implicit event APIs. Terminal solvers stop at the first bracketed root; vector
  solvers localize multiple detected crossings on the original dense interpolant.
  Optional tangency minimization also runs per scan interval when `tangenttol` is set.
- Add optional CPU `eventdepth` refinement to explicit and implicit terminal,
  vector and hybrid event APIs. Each level bisects configured scan intervals;
  combined work is capped at 4096 intervals per accepted step and default scan
  behavior remains unchanged.
- Add CPU `ODEHYBRID` and `IMPLICITHYBRID` for bounded scalar-guard state resets.
  Event records preserve pre/post-reset states at a shared timestamp, and the
  explicit six-impact ball workload now uses native event restarts instead of a
  fabricated epsilon-time advance. Finite event scans and interpolation limits
  still apply.

- Keep the windowed graphical installer within small displays using a bounded
  primary-display probe and per-process Qt scaling. Accept the real window
  frame bounds and avoid early-exit grep pipelines in installer launch checks.
  Revision 18 graphical BIOS installation passed; this layout correction is
  development source and still requires a rebuilt image.

- Build a private revision 18 workstation candidate from one frozen source;
  retain package/image identity and disposable VM acceptance evidence. Correct
  ISO validation to extract the tracked ALSA restore rule before comparison;
  cover that path in the ISO fixture regression.

- Add Ed25519-signed package-pair update metadata, safe administrator-owned
  public-key loading, expiry/revocation checks and retained authorization.
  A configured key store requires signatures for forward updates without
  blocking rollback/recovery. Add an offline publisher tool; no production key
  is generated or installed. Legacy checksum mode remains explicitly warned.

- Harden root administration requests: atomically publish private window-ID
  markers and validate held nonblocking, non-following descriptors before root
  reads them. Reject wrong owners, unsafe modes, links, special files and
  replacements during validation. Retain the trusted-operator security model;
  this does not isolate hostile applications from the shared root X11 terminal.

- Add separate per-session BASIC prompt recovery snapshots, AUTOSAVE controls
  and explicit RECOVER/EDIT discovery. Preserve unfinished drafts and originals;
  report checkpoint failures without blocking editing. Unhandled execution
  errors retain bounded statement, procedure and library context with hints for
  common mistakes, while preserving Error values and ON ERROR semantics.

- Require the appliance target, audio supervisor and a responding private audio
  server before committing desktop updates. Clear audio service start limits
  when restarting after installation or rollback.

- Add repeatable installed-system lifecycle acceptance on a new disposable disk:
  normal firmware boot, token-bound saved-state checks, supervised service
  recovery, offline package commit/rollback and guest-confirmed shutdown.
  Persistence verification now fails on missing files instead of recreating them.

- Keep virtual PCI audio outputs awake between sounds to avoid suspend/reopen
  glitches, preserve exact failed-service names in diagnostic reports, repair
  Debian's duplicate ALSA restore-rule label without overriding local rules,
  and exercise actual program-window bounds in live close/audio acceptance.

- Stream native music from queued note events instead of rendering complete
  tracks and a WAV before playback. Keep envelopes, oscillator phases, filters,
  waveguides and per-note settings across bounded audio blocks. Stream mixed
  native/SoundFont scores through the same output process, add a bounded device
  buffer, and retain WAV generation for explicit export. Check long-score
  startup, PCM equivalence, and paced playback continuity.
  Keep appliance/player gain at unity; save loudness corrections in BASIC
  scores. Use a configurable 250 ms device buffer for VM scheduling jitter,
  with regression checks for literal argument forwarding and session overrides.

- Add broadcast batched `TMM` and differentiable `TCONV1D`/`TCONV2D` with
  explicit stride, symmetric padding and dilation. Bound forward/backward work,
  retain gradients on failed backward passes, and validate against independent
  NumPy contractions and finite differences. Connect numeric lists and DIM-array
  snapshots directly to `WAVE`; add image/geometry, music and learned-filter
  applications plus a concrete math completion roadmap.

- Add `SYMREFINE` for conditional real simplification with exact sign deductions,
  square-root branches, inverse compositions and contradiction checks. Preserve
  original domains and explicit assumptions. Require suitable neighborhoods for
  calculus on guarded results, so a pointwise equality cannot create a false
